rows.name: Answering questions on a fantasy story
steps: Suggested: Read the fantasy story aloud to the circle, showing the pictures.
Suggested: Ask three factual questions, such as who is in the story and what happens first.
Suggested: Ask one opinion question, for example: Do you think Aqsa likes to play with dolls? Why?
Suggested: Ask each child to say what happened in the story in order.
Suggested: Note each answer and each reason on the class sheet.

levels.0: Answers to the factual questions are missing or unrelated to the fantasy story.
levels.1: Factual answers about who and what happened are right, but the opinion about a character comes with no reason.
levels.2: Events of the fantasy story are retold in order, with the right characters and what each one did.
levels.3: Opinions about a character come with a reason that points to a line or picture in the story.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B4; steps are suggested from the activity name. Reviewer asked for factual and opinion answers; linked LO is the retell, so level 2 follows the retell.

rows.name: Dictation (first introduction)
steps: Suggested: Seat children with notebooks and pencils and ask for quiet listening.
Suggested: Say one short word or sentence slowly, twice.
Suggested: Ask children to write it as they heard it.
Suggested: Say it once more so children can check what they wrote.
Suggested: Show the correct spelling on the board and let children tick or fix their own.

levels.0: Notebook lines stay blank or hold letters unrelated to the dictated words.
levels.1: Dictated words are written with the first sounds right but vowels or endings missing.
levels.2: Each word in the dictated sentence is written with correct spelling.
levels.3: A longer sentence dictated for the first time is written with correct spellings, a capital letter and a full stop.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic. First introduction, so words are kept short.

rows.name: Word Wall and Word of the Day
steps: Suggested: Pick a wall space and label it Word Wall.
Suggested: Write the Word of the Day on a card and read it with the class.
Suggested: Ask children what they think it means and give an example.
Suggested: Fix the card on the Word Wall.
Suggested: Ask each child to say or write one sentence using the word.

levels.0: Nothing is said or written with the Word of the Day by the end of the lesson.
levels.1: Word of the Day is copied from the Word Wall or said in a phrase without a full sentence.
levels.2: A sentence of the child's own contains the Word of the Day and makes sense.
levels.3: Word of the Day is used in a new sentence and its meaning is explained with an example.

rows.note: Routine. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Daily class diary notes
steps: Suggested: Agree one thing that happened in class today.
Suggested: Write the date and a sentence about the class event in the diary.
Suggested: Add one describing word.
Suggested: Read the sentence aloud to a partner.
Suggested: Keep diary notes to class events, not home or feelings.

levels.0: Diary page has a date, if anything, but no sentence about the day.
levels.1: One sentence about the day is written, or a drawing shows only a label.
levels.2: Two or three sentences in the diary tell what happened during the day.
levels.3: Diary sentences are joined by words such as then or because and tell events in the order they happened.

rows.note: Routine. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic. Reworded so the activity runs without recording a child's health, feelings, home or family data.

rows.name: Number games with Ganit Mala, beads and counters
steps: Suggested: Seat children in groups with a Ganit Mala, Base 10 beads and counters.
Suggested: Count together from 1 to 50, sliding one bead for each number said.
Suggested: Ask one child to start from any number on the Ganit Mala and count on.
Suggested: Group counters in sets of 2, 5 or 10 and count by the set.
Suggested: Count backwards from 20, sliding the beads back.
rows.materials: Introduction to Ganit Mala; Base 10 Beads; Counters

levels.0: Counting on the Ganit Mala stops before ten or skips beads without a number said.
levels.1: Counting from 1 reaches 50, but beginning from a middle number such as 23 breaks down.
levels.2: Beads are counted aloud forwards and backwards from any starting number within the range reached.
levels.3: Counting continues past 50 toward 100, or changes to counting in sets of 5, without going back to one.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C4; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Say, read and write numbers up to 10
steps: Suggested: Give each pair counters and number cards from 1 to 10.
Suggested: Show one card and ask children to say the number aloud.
Suggested: Ask them to lay out that many counters.
Suggested: Ask them to write the numeral in their notebook beside the counters.
Suggested: Mix the cards and repeat, then read the written numbers back.

levels.0: Number cards from 1 to 10 are left unread or named with the wrong number.
levels.1: Single-digit cards are read correctly, but the card 10 is read as one and zero.
levels.2: Numerals 1 to 10 are read aloud correctly when shown on cards, including 10 as two digits.
levels.3: Numbers such as 12 or 15 on cards not seen before are read aloud by looking at both digits.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C4; steps are suggested from the activity name. Linked LO is about 2-digit numbers; this activity stops at 10, so 10 is the 2-digit case in level 2.

rows.name: Greedy Crocodile: comparing numbers with <, > and =
steps: Tell the story of the Greedy Crocodile whose mouth always eats the bigger number.
Make a <, > alligator mouth from a paper plate.
Flash two numbers; children show the correct comparison with the mouth.
Move from numbers under 20 to under 50, then two-digit against two-digit.
Fill in the missing signs on the worksheet.
rows.materials: Flashcards, paper plates, alligator craft, number strips

levels.0: No sign appears between the two numbers, or one sign is used for every pair.
levels.1: Signs are placed between pairs, but the open side points to the smaller number in some pairs.
levels.2: Both signs < and > and the = sign are placed correctly between each pair of 2-digit numbers.
levels.3: A new pair with the same tens, such as 47 and 43, is compared and the tens-then-ones reason is said.

rows.name: Odd and even with counters, hopscotch and Odd-Even Monsters
steps: Warm up by counting 1–20 together.
Each child picks a number card and places counters in pairs under it.
If all counters pair up the number is even; if one is left over it is odd.
Sort the cards into two group charts, Odd and Even.
Play odd-even hopscotch: jump only on odd or only on even numbers.
Make an Odd-Even Monster: the odd monster has 1 eye, the even monster has 2 eyes.
rows.materials: Counters, number cards 1–50, chart paper, crayons, worksheets

levels.0: Counters are not paired up, and numbers are not named as odd or even.
levels.1: Counters are paired, but a lone counter left over is not linked to the word odd.
levels.2: Numbers are named odd or even by pairing counters, with a left-over counter marking an odd number.
levels.3: A larger number such as 17 is named odd or even by thinking of pairs, without counters.

rows.name: Recognising and writing vowels अ to औ
steps: Suggested: Show the vowel chart from अ to औ and say each letter aloud for children to repeat.
Suggested: Play the two linked videos on the vowels.
Suggested: Say a sound and ask children to point to the matching letter on the chart.
Suggested: Ask children to trace each vowel in the air, then write it in the notebook.
Suggested: Walk round and check each vowel against the chart.

levels.0: Notebook page has no vowel from अ to औ written, or only marks that cannot be read as letters.
levels.1: Vowels are written, but several lack the top line or have a wrong curve.
levels.2: Each vowel from अ to औ is written with its correct shape in the notebook.
levels.3: Vowels are written in order from memory when the educator calls them out in a mixed order.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D4; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Retelling a story (पुनः प्रयास और कहानी सुनाना)
steps: Suggested: Tell a short Hindi story, showing a picture for each main event.
Suggested: Ask what happened first, next and last.
Suggested: Hand pairs the picture cards and ask them to put them in order.
Suggested: Ask each child to retell the story to a partner in Hindi.
Suggested: Listen in and note who tells the events in order.

levels.0: No retelling is given, or only the title of the story is said.
levels.1: Some events are told but out of order, or only with picture prompts.
levels.2: Story is retold in own Hindi words with the events in order.
levels.3: A story heard once is retold in order, with a detail of the child's own added.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Talking about my school (अपनी पाठशाला के बारे में बातें)
steps: Suggested: Sit in a circle and ask what we can see in our school.
Suggested: Write a sentence starter on the board: मेरी पाठशाला में ... है।
Suggested: Ask each child to say three sentences about the school.
Suggested: Ask a partner to repeat one thing they heard.
Suggested: Note who speaks in Hindi without switching to English.

levels.0: No Hindi sentence about the school is spoken.
levels.1: One or two Hindi words, or a single sentence mixed with English, are said about the school.
levels.2: Three or more Hindi sentences about the school are spoken.
levels.3: Hindi sentences about the school include a reason or a feeling, such as मुझे ... अच्छा लगता है क्योंकि ...

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: About the senses scrapbook
steps: Suggested: Look at pictures of the senses in books and magazines.
Suggested: Cut and paste a picture for each of the five senses on a scrapbook page.
Suggested: Label each picture with the sense word.
Suggested: Write one sentence about what a sense is used for.
Suggested: Display the finished pages in class.

levels.0: Scrapbook pages have no sense named, and no sense organ is labelled.
levels.1: A sense organ is drawn in the scrapbook, but the matching sense word is missing or swapped.
levels.2: Scrapbook page names the sense used in each tried activity, such as smelling or tasting.
levels.3: Scrapbook page links a new object to the sense used and to the body part that does it.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G4; steps are suggested from the activity name. Project named in the cell; station detail is added from the theme. Reworded so the activity runs without recording a child's health, feelings, home or family data.

rows.name: Directions puzzle
steps: Suggested: Draw a simple school or classroom map on chart paper.
Suggested: Teach left, right, near and far with body actions.
Suggested: Give pairs puzzle cards with clues such as: the book is on the left of the bag.
Suggested: Ask one child to read a clue while the partner places the object on the map.
Suggested: Swap roles and let each child make up a clue.

levels.0: No direction word is used while placing things in the puzzle.
levels.1: Left and right are used but sometimes swapped when placing objects on the puzzle.
levels.2: Left, right, near and far are used correctly to place things in the puzzle.
levels.3: Directions for a new route are given and a partner reaches the place by following them.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Songs on water and action songs
steps: Suggested: Teach the water song line by line, with the children repeating each line.
Suggested: Add an action for each line and practise slowly.
Suggested: Sing the song together, then a little faster.
Suggested: Teach the action song in the same way.
Suggested: Finish with a short art and craft task linked to the songs.

levels.0: Both the words and the actions of the water song are missing when the group sings.
levels.1: Words of the song are sung, but the actions lag behind or are copied from a neighbour.
levels.2: Song words and actions match in time with the group from the first line to the last.
levels.3: Actions are led for a new verse or a second song while the group follows.

rows.note: Cultural immersion. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Paper folding: square, diagonal, horizontal, vertical
steps: Suggested: Give each child four sheets of paper.
Suggested: Show the horizontal fold: edge to edge across the middle; children copy it.
Suggested: Show the vertical fold in the same way, then the diagonal fold corner to corner.
Suggested: Show how to fold a rectangle into a square.
Suggested: Ask children to open each sheet and look at the crease.

levels.0: Folded sheets show no crease lines, or all four folds look the same.
levels.1: Two of the four folds, such as horizontal and vertical, make clear creases that meet edge to edge.
levels.2: Square, diagonal, horizontal and vertical folds each show a sharp crease and matching edges.
levels.3: A new shape such as a triangle or rectangle is folded and named by the folds used.

rows.note: Steps built out from the educators' one-line list. Steps are suggested, not copied from the source.

rows.name: Paper cat, dog, mouse, fan and fish
steps: Suggested: Hand out paper and show the first linked video.
Suggested: Fold the cat step by step as the educator shows, then add the face.
Suggested: Fold the dog and the mouse in the same way.
Suggested: Fold the fan and the fish.
Suggested: Display all five objects on a table.
rows.materials: Paper; the cell links a video for each (links not copied)

levels.0: No folded animal or fan is finished, and sheets show only loose creases.
levels.1: Some of the five objects are folded, with corners that do not meet and loose creases.
levels.2: Cat, dog, mouse, fan and fish each hold their shape with corners meeting.
levels.3: A new paper object is folded from picture steps seen for the first time.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!H4; steps are suggested from the activity name. Five objects named in one cell; the cell links a video for each (links not copied).

rows.name: Picture-based story telling
steps: Suggested: Place four or five picture cards in a row in story order.
Suggested: Ask what is happening in each picture.
Suggested: Ask children to tell the story card by card.
Suggested: Mix the cards, let a child put them back in order and tell the story again.
Suggested: Ask pairs to tell the story to each other.

levels.0: Picture cards are set out, but no sentence is said about any picture.
levels.1: Each picture gets a word or phrase, but the sentences do not link into a story.
levels.2: Story is told from the picture cards in own words, with each picture in order.
levels.3: Cards are shuffled and reordered, then the story is told with an added detail not in the pictures.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Making flashcards
steps: Suggested: Give each child six blank cards.
Suggested: Ask them to write a word from the unit on each card.
Suggested: Ask them to draw a matching picture on the other side.
Suggested: Check the spelling against the Word Wall.
Suggested: Ask children to swap cards with a partner and read each other's words.

levels.0: Blank card stays blank, or shows a picture without any word.
levels.1: Cards hold a word and a picture, but the picture does not match or the word is misspelt.
levels.2: Each flashcard shows a word and a matching picture for it.
levels.3: A new word from the day's story is made into a flashcard that a partner reads correctly.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Skip counting: songs, beads, giant number line, Lego tower
steps: Sing skip-counting songs for 2s, 5s and 10s.
String bead bracelets in sets of 2, 5 or 10.
Hop along a giant floor number line counting by 2s, 5s and 10s.
Build a Skip Count Tower with Lego: 2 red blocks, 2 blue blocks and so on.
Advanced: count backward by the same steps.
rows.materials: Number lines, jump ropes, beads, coloured markers, Lego blocks

levels.0: Counting by 2s, 5s or 10s breaks off at the first number or turns into counting by ones.
levels.1: Counting in 10s runs smoothly from zero, but counting in 2s or 5s loses its place.
levels.2: Skip counting in 2s, 5s and 10s runs aloud from zero to 20 or beyond without losing step.
levels.3: Counting in 5s starts from a number such as 15 and reaches 50 in order.

rows.note: Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!C4.

rows.name: 2D and 3D shapes on a geo board
steps: Suggested: Give each child a geo board and bands.
Suggested: Ask children to make a square, a rectangle and a triangle with the bands, and name each.
Suggested: Ask them to make a pentagon and a hexagon.
Suggested: Show the Jodo Blocks and Froebel's Gifts and ask children to name the shape on each face.
Suggested: Sort the shapes made into 2D and 3D.
rows.materials: Geo board; Jodo Blocks; Froebel's Gifts

levels.0: Shapes made on the geo board stay unnamed, or are named by an object such as door.
levels.1: Square, triangle and circle are named correctly, but rectangle, pentagon or hexagon are confused.
levels.2: Square, circle, triangle, rectangle, hexagon and pentagon are each named when shown.
levels.3: A shape built with bands on the geo board is named and its sides are counted aloud.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Addition and subtraction on a number line
steps: Suggested: Draw a number line from 0 to 20 on the floor or on paper strips.
Suggested: Model 5 + 3 by jumping forward three places from 5.
Suggested: Model 8 - 3 by jumping back three places from 8.
Suggested: Give sums and ask children to draw the jumps on their strips.
Suggested: Ask children to write the number sentence under each drawing.
rows.materials: Number line (link to twinkl number-line page in cell); StoryWeaver addition lesson plan link in cell

levels.0: No jumps are drawn on the number line for the sums.
levels.1: Jumps are drawn but miscounted by one, or start from the wrong number.
levels.2: Each jump is drawn and the answer is correct for adding and taking away.
levels.3: A word problem is turned into a number-line drawing that gives the right answer.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C5; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Show & Tell Project #1
steps: Suggested: Ask each child to bring or make something that shows a maths idea, such as a number chart, a shape model or a counting game.
Suggested: Set up a table to display the items.
Suggested: Ask each child to show their item to the class.
Suggested: Ask them to say in a sentence what it shows.
Suggested: Let the class ask one question to each presenter.

levels.0: Nothing is shown to the class, or the item brought has no link to maths.
levels.1: A model or chart is shown, but only named as a thing, without a maths idea.
levels.2: A maths idea made by the child is shown and what it shows is said in a sentence.
levels.3: A question from classmates about the maths idea is answered with an example.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C5; steps are suggested from the activity name. Cell names the project only; steps built from the name and unit. Linked to the nearest existing LO; the Show & Tell cell names no maths content. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!C4.

rows.name: Recognising and writing क to झ
steps: Suggested: Show the consonant chart from क to झ and say each letter aloud.
Suggested: Ask children to repeat and point to each letter as it is said.
Suggested: Ask them to trace each letter in the air.
Suggested: Ask children to write each letter in the notebook with its top line.
Suggested: Read the letters back together.

levels.0: Notebook lines have no consonant from क to झ, or only scribbles.
levels.1: Consonants are written, but several miss the top line or reverse a curve.
levels.2: Every consonant from क to झ is written with its correct shape in the notebook.
levels.3: Consonants are written in a new order from the educator's spoken sounds, without the chart.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D5; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Oral practice: my favourite fruit, my favourite journey
steps: Suggested: Bring pictures of fruits and journeys such as a bus or a train ride.
Suggested: Model three Hindi sentences about a favourite fruit.
Suggested: Ask each child to speak about their favourite fruit.
Suggested: Ask each child to speak about their favourite journey.
Suggested: Ask a partner to repeat one sentence they heard.

levels.0: No Hindi sentence is spoken on the favourite fruit or the favourite journey.
levels.1: A few Hindi words on one topic are said, and the other topic is left out.
levels.2: Three or more Hindi sentences are spoken on the favourite fruit and on the favourite journey.
levels.3: Talk about the fruit or journey gives a reason for the choice and one describing word.

rows.note: Speaking practice. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Making my own fantasy story with beginning, middle and end
steps: Suggested: Retell a short fantasy story and mark its beginning, middle and end on a three-part chart.
Suggested: Ask each child to fold paper into three boxes.
Suggested: Ask them to choose a magic character and a place.
Suggested: Ask them to write the beginning and the middle.
Suggested: Ask them to write the ending in two or three sentences.
Suggested: Ask children to read their story to a partner.

levels.0: Story page has no ending, and the three boxes hold only a beginning or nothing.
levels.1: An ending sentence is written but does not follow from the middle of the story.
levels.2: Story ends with two or three sentences that settle the problem set up in the middle.
levels.3: Beginning, middle and end are all written, and the ending links back to the opening problem.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B11; steps are suggested from the activity name. LO 0204 is the story-ending LO; closest match.

rows.name: Make my own number game
steps: Suggested: Show a sample number game such as a dice race or number snap.
Suggested: Give out card, dice, counters and paper.
Suggested: Ask children to make a board or cards and write the rules.
Suggested: Ask them to test the game with a partner.
Suggested: Ask them to change one rule and play again.

levels.0: No game board, cards or rules exist at the end of the lesson.
levels.1: A game board or cards exist, but the rules are unclear to a partner.
levels.2: A partner can play the number game from the rules given.
levels.3: One rule is changed and the change in play is described.

rows.note: Cell names the activity only; steps built from the name and unit.

rows.name: Writing numbers 1 to 50 in the square notebook
steps: Suggested: Give each child a square notebook.
Suggested: Show how one digit goes in each square.
Suggested: Write 1 to 10 together on the board.
Suggested: Ask children to write the numbers to 50 in rows of ten.
Suggested: Ask partners to read each row aloud to each other.

levels.0: Square notebook rows stop before 10, or digits sit outside the squares.
levels.1: Numbers are written to 50, but some digits are reversed or numbers are missed.
levels.2: Numbers 1 to 50 are written in order, one digit per square, and read aloud from the page.
levels.3: Writing continues beyond 50 and the numbers are read aloud, ten at a time, without a model.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Revision of skip counting in 2s, 5s, 10s
steps: Suggested: Stand in a circle and clap while counting in 2s.
Suggested: Count in 5s, hopping on each fifth number.
Suggested: Count in 10s, raising a hand on each ten.
Suggested: Give a blank hundred chart and ask children to colour the 2s, 5s and 10s in three colours.
Suggested: Ask what they notice about the coloured numbers.

levels.0: Coloured squares on the hundred chart do not follow any skip-counting pattern.
levels.1: Squares for 10s are coloured correctly, while 2s and 5s have missed or extra numbers.
levels.2: Counting aloud and the coloured chart both show 2s, 5s and 10s from zero in the right order.
levels.3: A pattern on the chart is explained, such as all numbers counted in 5s ending in 0 or 5.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!C4.

rows.name: Extending patterns to numbers
steps: Suggested: Show a pattern made of beads or colours and ask children to say what comes next.
Suggested: Replace the colours with numbers, such as 2, 4, 6.
Suggested: Ask what the rule is.
Suggested: Give cards such as 3, 6, 9 and ask children to write the next three numbers.
Suggested: Ask each child to make a number pattern for a partner to continue.

levels.0: Number pattern strips are left without any following number written.
levels.1: Next number is written correctly, but the following two break the rule.
levels.2: Next three numbers of the pattern are written by following its rule.
levels.3: A rule for a new pattern is said aloud, and the pattern is extended or made for a partner.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Observing patterns in the calendar and solving calendar problems
steps: Suggested: Put up the month calendar and find today's date and day name.
Suggested: Look at a column and notice that dates go up by seven each row.
Suggested: Ask questions such as: what is the date next Monday, and how many Sundays are there?
Suggested: Ask children to find a date called out by the educator.
Suggested: Ask pairs to make up a calendar question for another pair.

levels.0: A given date such as the 12th is not located on the calendar.
levels.1: Right row is found for a date, but the wrong day-name column.
levels.2: Given date is found on the calendar and its day name is read.
levels.3: Calendar questions such as the date one week later are answered by looking down the column.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Calligraphy practice (सुलेख माला) and revising इ, ई
steps: Suggested: Write इ and ई on the board and say their sounds.
Suggested: Ask children to trace both letters in the air.
Suggested: Show the सुलेख माला page and the line each letter sits on.
Suggested: Ask children to practise writing the letters on the सुलेख माला lines.
Suggested: Check shape and size on the line for each child.

levels.0: Practice lines show no इ or ई written, only strokes with no letter shape.
levels.1: Both letters are written, but the top line is missing or the loop of ई is open.
levels.2: Both इ and ई are written on the सुलेख माला lines with their correct shapes.
levels.3: इ and ई are written correctly inside a new word from memory, with even size on the line.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Looking at pictures in the vowels book and introducing ए, ऐ
steps: Suggested: Open the vowels book and look at the pictures for ए and ऐ.
Suggested: Ask children to say a few things about each picture.
Suggested: Say the picture words and stress their first sound.
Suggested: Show the letters ए and ऐ and ask children to say each sound.
Suggested: Ask children to trace the letters in the air.

levels.0: Letters ए and ऐ are shown but no sound is said, or the sound of another vowel is given.
levels.1: Sound of ए is said correctly, but ऐ is mixed up with it.
levels.2: Sounds of ए and ऐ are each said correctly when the letter is shown.
levels.3: A new picture word from the vowels book is linked to ए or ऐ by its first sound.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Learning the new poem 'एक छोटी कश्ती मेरे पास'
steps: Suggested: Play the linked video of the poem 'एक छोटी कश्ती मेरे पास'.
Suggested: Say the poem line by line and ask children to repeat each line.
Suggested: Add an action for each line.
Suggested: Recite the whole poem together, then in groups.
Suggested: Invite volunteers to recite it alone.

levels.0: No line of the poem is recited aloud by the child or the group.
levels.1: Some lines are recited, with words missed or mixed.
levels.2: Poem is recited with all the words right.
levels.3: Recitation of the poem includes expression and actions that fit its words.

rows.note: LO link is an assumption from the unit and siblings. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: A patriotic story and talk about Independence Day
steps: Suggested: Show a picture of the flag and ask what day is 15 August.
Suggested: Tell a short patriotic story (देश भक्ति की कहानी).
Suggested: Talk about what people do on Independence Day.
Suggested: Ask each child to say a sentence about the day in Hindi.
Suggested: Ask a few children to tell one part of the story.

levels.0: Independence Day passes in the talk with no Hindi word spoken about it.
levels.1: One Hindi word or phrase about the day is said.
levels.2: One full Hindi sentence about Independence Day is spoken.
levels.3: Two or more Hindi sentences are spoken, one telling what happens in the patriotic story.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Know and make national symbols
steps: Suggested: Show pictures of the national symbols: flag, tiger, peacock, lotus and emblem.
Suggested: Name each symbol and ask children to repeat it.
Suggested: Ask children to make the symbols with paper and colours, such as the tricolour flag.
Suggested: Ask children to label each symbol.
Suggested: Display the symbols on a board.

levels.0: Symbol pictures are shown, but none is named or labelled.
levels.1: Flag is named, but other symbols such as the peacock or lotus are unnamed or swapped.
levels.2: National symbols in pictures, such as the flag, peacock, tiger and lotus, are named correctly.
levels.3: A symbol made by the child is labelled and what it stands for is said.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G11; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Watercolour activity on water
steps: Suggested: Talk about where we see water: rain, river, tap.
Suggested: Show how to wet the brush and mix watercolour.
Suggested: Ask children to paint a picture of water being used.
Suggested: Ask them to label what the water is used for.
Suggested: Share paintings in pairs.

levels.0: Painting shows water but no use of water is named.
levels.1: One use of water, such as drinking, is named, and the second is missing.
levels.2: Two uses of water at home or school, such as drinking and washing, are named or painted.
levels.3: A use of water not in the painting, such as for plants, is added and why it matters is said.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G11; steps are suggested from the activity name. Cell names a watercolour activity on water only; linked LO (uses of water) is the closest match but the painting may not show it.

rows.name: Representation of My Neighbourhood
steps: Suggested: Name places in the neighbourhood together: shop, park, temple, school.
Suggested: Ask children to say what each place is used for.
Suggested: Give a large sheet and ask children to draw or paste the places along a route.
Suggested: Ask children to label each place.
Suggested: Show the neighbourhood to the class.

levels.0: Neighbourhood drawing shows no named place and no label on any building.
levels.1: Places are drawn, but their use is not told.
levels.2: Each local place in the picture is named and its use is said, such as shop for buying.
levels.3: A place is added from a different part of the neighbourhood and located next to another.

rows.note: Art cell; linked to GP LO 0415 because G1 art LOs sit under Global perspectives. Steps built from the name and unit.

rows.name: Thread knots: eco rakhi making
steps: Suggested: Show a sample eco rakhi and its knots.
Suggested: Give each child a length of thread.
Suggested: Show how to tie a knot, then ask children to tie their own.
Suggested: Add a natural item chosen by the educator to the thread.
Suggested: Pull each knot gently to check it holds.

levels.0: No knot is tied in the rakhi thread.
levels.1: A knot is tied but comes undone when pulled.
levels.2: A knot holds when the rakhi thread is pulled.
levels.3: Two knots are tied neatly so the rakhi fits the wrist.

rows.note: LO link is an assumption from the unit and siblings. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Paper puppets of the sense organs
steps: Suggested: Name the five sense organs together: eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin.
Suggested: Give each child paper.
Suggested: Show how to fold the paper to make a puppet base.
Suggested: Ask children to draw and cut one sense organ for the puppet.
Suggested: Ask each child to show the puppet and say its sense.

levels.0: Paper stays flat, with no fold or puppet shape made.
levels.1: Paper is folded once, but the puppet base does not hold its shape.
levels.2: A folded paper puppet holds its shape and shows a sense organ.
levels.3: Puppet for a second sense organ is made by folding, and its sense is named.

rows.note: LO link is an assumption from the unit and siblings. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Enhanced Senses (project-based learning)
steps: Suggested: Set up simple stations for smell, taste, touch, sound and sight.
Suggested: Ask children to try each station in turn.
Suggested: Ask them to say which sense they used.
Suggested: Ask them to tick a record sheet for each station.
Suggested: Ask children to share what they found out.

levels.0: Record sheet has no sense named for any station.
levels.1: Sense organ is pointed to, but the sense word is left out or swapped.
levels.2: Sense used at each station, such as smelling or tasting, is named after trying it.
levels.3: A new object is tried and the sense that tells most about it is named with a reason.

rows.note: Cell names the project only; linked to the senses LO. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Animal guessing game
steps: Suggested: Pick an animal card in secret.
Suggested: Say one clue about the animal.
Suggested: Ask the others to guess.
Suggested: Add one more clue after each wrong guess.
Suggested: Swap so another child gives the clues.

levels.0: No clue about the animal is given before others start guessing.
levels.1: One clue is given and others cannot guess.
levels.2: Clues, two or three in number, let others guess the animal.
levels.3: Clues use describing words (size, colour, sound) so the animal is guessed in three tries.

rows.note: Speaking skill. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Shape hunt and Shape City
steps: Pass round 3D shapes (cube, sphere, cylinder) and 2D shapes (square, triangle, circle) and name them.
Go on a shape hunt around school.
Make a Shape City from cut-out shapes: houses, cars, traffic lights.
Sort the shapes into 2D and 3D.
Make 3D shapes from playdough.
rows.materials: Shape cut-outs, building blocks, playdough, chart paper, box, ball, tin

levels.0: Built solids stay unnamed, or are called by the 2D shape on one face.
levels.1: Cube and cuboid are named, but cone, sphere or cylinder are mixed up.
levels.2: Cube, cuboid, sphere, cone and cylinder are each named when the solid is shown.
levels.3: A solid built from 2D shapes is named and the shapes forming its faces are counted.

rows.name: Ten-frame board and counters: numbers up to 100
steps: Suggested: Give each pair a ten-frame board and counters.
Suggested: Show a number such as 14 by filling one frame and four more places.
Suggested: Use several frames to build numbers up to 100.
Suggested: Ask children to say the number aloud, counting tens then ones.
Suggested: Ask partners to count back from the number built.

levels.0: Frames hold counters, but the number built is not said or is said wrongly.
levels.1: Full frames are counted in tens, but the leftover counters are counted incorrectly.
levels.2: On the ten-frames, counters are counted aloud forwards and backwards from a chosen number up to 100.
levels.3: Ten-frames show a new number such as 68, built and counted on from 60 without starting at one.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C12; steps are suggested from the activity name.

rows.name: Estimation: guess, count, how far
steps: Suggested: Show a jar of counters or an object on the floor and ask for a guess of how many or how far.
Suggested: Write each guess on a slip.
Suggested: Count the counters, or measure the distance in hand spans or steps.
Suggested: Compare each guess with the count.
Suggested: Say whether the guess was too high or too low.

levels.0: Guess slips are blank, and nothing is counted or measured to check them.
levels.1: A guess is recorded and the count is made, but the measuring units leave gaps.
levels.2: A length is measured in non-standard units, and the count is compared with the earlier guess.
levels.3: Second guess after the first measurement gets closer, with a reason such as measuring one unit first.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C12; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps read from 'guess, counting & how far'.

rows.name: Speaking on my favourite fruit and drawing it
steps: Suggested: Show a fruit and say its Hindi name.
Suggested: Ask children to say two or three sentences about their favourite fruit.
Suggested: Ask them to draw the fruit in the copy.
Suggested: Ask each child to show the drawing and speak about it.

levels.0: The copy has no drawing of the fruit and nothing is said about it.
levels.1: A drawing is made, with only a word or two said.
levels.2: Fruit is described in two or three sentences, and the drawing shows it.
levels.3: Talk names the fruit's colour, taste and why it is liked.

rows.note: Speaking. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Telling the difference between vowels and consonants
steps: Suggested: Display letter cards of Hindi vowels and consonants.
Suggested: Say that a स्वर can stand alone as a sound and a व्यंजन needs a vowel.
Suggested: Give pairs a set of cards and two hoops or boxes labelled स्वर and व्यंजन.
Suggested: Ask pairs to sort the cards into the two groups.
Suggested: Ask a child to say how they decided for one card.

levels.0: Letter cards are left unsorted, with none placed under स्वर or व्यंजन.
levels.1: Some letter cards are sorted with errors, such as क placed under स्वर.
levels.2: All given letters are correctly sorted into स्वर and व्यंजन.
levels.3: A new set is sorted and the difference is said (a स्वर stands alone).

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D12; steps are suggested from the activity name.

rows.name: Introducing क and ख and drawing pictures that start with them
steps: Suggested: Show क and ख on the board and say their sounds.
Suggested: Ask children to trace the letters in the air and then write them in the notebook.
Suggested: Think of picture words that begin with each, such as कमल and खरगोश.
Suggested: Ask children to draw a few pictures for each letter.
Suggested: Ask them to write the letter beside each picture.

levels.0: Notebook has no क or ख written beside any picture.
levels.1: Letters क and ख are written, but ख has a wrong curve or misses its top line.
levels.2: Both क and ख are written with the correct shape beside pictures whose names begin with them.
levels.3: A picture word starting with क or ख that was not given is thought of, drawn and labelled with its letter.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D12; the cell is a one-line topic (or a topic plus links), so the steps are suggested.

rows.name: Dictation of 8 words
steps: Suggested: Ask children to number a notebook page from 1 to 8.
Suggested: Say the first word twice, slowly.
Suggested: Ask children to write it, then move to the next word.
Suggested: Read all eight words once more so children can check.
Suggested: Correct the words together and ask children to count how many are right.
Suggested: Dictate one short sentence that uses three of the eight words.

levels.0: The dictated sentence is not written, or fewer than three of its words appear.
levels.1: The sentence is written, but two or more of the list words in it have missing or swapped letters.
levels.2: The dictated sentence is written with every word spelt correctly.
levels.3: A new dictated sentence using two other list words is written correctly, with a capital letter and a full stop.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B16; steps are suggested from the activity name.

rows.name: Show & Tell
steps: Suggested: Ask children to bring one object they like.
Suggested: Place a table at the front for the objects.
Suggested: Ask each child to say two or three sentences about their object.
Suggested: Let the class ask one question to each speaker.
Suggested: Thank each speaker before the next one.

levels.0: Silence follows when asked to tell the class about the object.
levels.1: Object is named in a word, with nothing said about why it was brought.
levels.2: Speech of two or three sentences tells what the object is and why it was brought.
levels.3: A question from the class is answered about the object.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Plurals by adding s and es; joining with 'and'
steps: Suggested: Show picture cards of one and many (cat, cats, box, boxes) and say each pair aloud.
Suggested: Write cat and cats on the board and circle the s ending.
Suggested: Write box, bus and dish and ask children to say what they hear at the end.
Suggested: Have children write the plural of each word in their notebooks, adding s or es.
Suggested: Give each pair two word cards joined with 'and' and ask them to write one sentence using both.

levels.0: Notebook lines for the plural task stay blank, with no word changed from one to many.
levels.1: Plurals such as cats and dogs have an s, but box and bus are left as box or written boxs.
levels.2: Both cats and boxes appear in the notebook, with s added to some words and es to others.
levels.3: Fox, church or glass, never taught in class, is written as foxes, churches or glasses and the ending rule is said aloud.

rows.note: Plural part is clear. The 'and' joining part has no linked LO and is kept as a short extension step. Steps built partly from the unit. Steps are suggested, not copied from the source.

rows.name: Writing numbers 50 to 100 in the square notebook
steps: Suggested: Give each child a square notebook and write 50 on the board.
Suggested: Count aloud together from 50 to 59 while children write each number, one digit per square.
Suggested: Continue in groups of ten up to 100, pausing to say each number aloud.
Suggested: Ask children to point to any number they wrote and read it to a partner.
Suggested: Collect notebooks and check that the digits are in the right order.

levels.0: Few or no numbers from 50 to 100 are written in the squares.
levels.1: Numbers are written, but several have digits reversed, such as 75 for 57, or some are skipped.
levels.2: Every number from 50 to 100 is written in order with the digits the right way round, one digit per square.
levels.3: Numbers the educator calls out of order, such as 91 or 68, are written correctly without looking at the chart.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the square notebook; the cell gave no routine.

rows.name: Before, after and between on the number line
steps: Suggested: Draw a number line from 40 to 70 on the board and give each child a printed line.
Suggested: Ask 'What comes just before 52?' and mark the answer with a finger on the line.
Suggested: Ask 'What comes just after 59?' and then 'What lies between 61 and 63?'.
Suggested: Have children colour the before, after and between numbers on their line.
Suggested: Give two numbers from the line and ask which is greater, writing <, > or = between them.

levels.0: Number line sheets show no jumps or marks, and before, after and between questions go unanswered.
levels.1: Jumps on the number line are drawn, but the landing number is miscounted by one or the start square is counted as a jump.
levels.2: On the number line the jumps land on the right number, and the sum or difference written matches the jumps.
levels.3: Jumps drawn on a blank line, with the educator's new start number, give a correct answer and a partner is told how the jumps were counted.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C16; steps are suggested from the activity name. Two LOs linked; rubric is about the first (jumping on a number line). Comparing is covered in G1-108.

rows.name: Revising अ to अः and calligraphy practice
steps: Suggested: Show the Hindi vowels अ to अः on a chart and say each sound aloud for children to repeat.
Suggested: Trace each letter in the air with a finger while saying its name.
Suggested: Give each child the सुलेख माला and ask them to copy each letter on the lines.
Suggested: Move around the room and show children where each letter starts and ends.
Suggested: Ask children to circle their best-formed letter in the notebook.

levels.0: सुलेख माला pages remain empty, with no vowel from अ to अः written.
levels.1: Letters from अ to अः are written but the shirorekha is missing or several letters sit outside the line.
levels.2: Each vowel from अ to अः is copied with its full shape, hangs from the line and is readable by the educator.
levels.3: Vowels written from dictation, without the chart, keep the same shape and line placement in a new notebook page.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the calligraphy book (सुलेख माला).

rows.name: Listen, sing and tell: rain (सुनो, गाओ और बताओ – वर्षा)
steps: Suggested: Play or sing the rain song (वर्षा) twice while children listen.
Suggested: Teach the song one line at a time, with children repeating each line.
Suggested: Sing the whole song together, with a hand movement for rain.
Suggested: Ask pairs to sing the song to each other and then to the group.
Suggested: Ask a few children to tell in one sentence what the song says about rain.

levels.0: Rain song lines are not sung, and the group song is met with silence.
levels.1: Opening lines of the rain song are sung, with later words skipped or replaced by humming.
levels.2: Every line of the rain song is sung with the right words, from first line to last.
levels.3: After singing, the song's story of rain is told in a sentence in the child's own Hindi words.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; the rain song itself is not named in the cell. Rubric covers singing; telling is a stretch.

rows.name: Sound sources, loud and quiet, sound moves
steps: Suggested: Walk around the classroom and school with eyes closed and name each sound heard.
Suggested: Collect sound makers (drum, bell, paper, pencil) and let each child try one.
Suggested: Play each object softly then loudly and ask children to say loud or quiet.
Suggested: Place two hoops marked loud and quiet and ask children to put each object in a hoop.
Suggested: Ask one child to move away from a sound and say what happens to the loudness.

levels.0: Loud and quiet hoops stay empty, and no sound source is named by the children.
levels.1: Sound makers are named, yet the bell is placed with the quiet ones and the soft paper with the loud ones.
levels.2: Each sound heard is placed in the loud hoop or the quiet hoop, with the source named, and most placements agree with the educator's.
levels.3: A drum moved nearer then farther is described, in the child's words, as louder then quieter.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G16; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and unit; the cell lists three topics. Rubric covers sorting loud and quiet. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!E16.

rows.name: Using a needle to create crafts
steps: Suggested: Show a needle and thread and explain where it goes and how to hold it safely.
Suggested: Give each child a piece of felt and a blunt plastic needle with thread.
Suggested: Ask children to pass the needle up and down to make a small craft shape, such as a Ganpati bookmark.
Suggested: Walk round and check each child's stitches.
Suggested: Ask children to hold up the finished piece and say one thing they sewed.

levels.0: Fabric squares stay unsewn, with no thread passed through them.
levels.1: Stitches appear in the cloth, but they bunch together or the thread pulls out at the first one.
levels.2: A row of stitches, spaced about the same distance apart, runs along the fabric in the over-and-under pattern.
levels.3: On a new shape, such as a Ganpati outline, the stitch line follows the edge and the child explains how the stitch goes.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G16; steps are suggested from the activity name. Cell does not say which craft; the craft shape is suggested and should be checked. Needle safety rules are assumed.

rows.name: Origami animals
steps: Watch the folds demonstrated.
Fold a simple animal in the same order.
Decorate it.

levels.0: Paper squares stay flat, with no fold made.
levels.1: A fold is made, but the corners do not meet and the crease is crumpled.
levels.2: A paper shape with sharp creases and matching corners, such as a triangle, is held up by the child.
levels.3: A second shape, such as a boat, is folded from a new sheet by copying the educator's steps in order.

rows.name: Hand sewing step 1: lacing
steps: Suggested: Show a lacing card with holes and a thick shoelace.
Suggested: Tie a knot in one end and thread the other end through the first hole.
Suggested: Give each child a card and ask them to lace in and out along the holes.
Suggested: Remind children to pull the lace gently, so the card does not bend.
Suggested: Check that the lace goes in each hole in turn.

levels.0: Lacing cards are handed back with the lace still unthreaded.
levels.1: Lace runs through the first few holes, but one or two holes are skipped in the middle.
levels.2: The lace passes through every hole in order, from the first to the last, with the card flat.
levels.3: A new lacing pattern, such as a zigzag or a flower, is laced and the in-and-out path is explained.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the step name. A lacing card is assumed, not named in the cell. needs_link: lacing is a preparation step; the running-stitch LO does not cover it (round 4 sweep).

rows.name: Hand sewing step 2: threading
steps: Suggested: Show a needle with a large eye and a length of thread.
Suggested: Wet one end of the thread and pinch it flat.
Suggested: Push the thread through the eye of the needle.
Suggested: Pull out about a hand span and tie a knot at the long end.
Suggested: Hold up the threaded needle for a check before sewing.

levels.0: Needle and thread are put down with the thread still outside the eye.
levels.1: The thread reaches the eye but slips out, so it is tried several times with a partner helping.
levels.2: Thread passes through the needle's eye and a knot sits at the long end of the thread.
levels.3: A new needle with a smaller eye is threaded and the steps are told to a classmate.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name; cell lists materials needle and thread only. needs_link: threading is a preparation step that no G1 objective covers.

rows.name: Hand sewing step 3: needle stitching
steps: Suggested: Show how to push the needle up from under the cloth and pull the thread through.
Suggested: Show the next stitch, going down then up a short distance away.
Suggested: Mark a line with dots on the cloth for each child.
Suggested: Ask children to sew along the dots, one stitch per dot.
Suggested: Look at the back of the work together to see the stitches.

levels.0: Dotted cloth stays unmarked by stitches, with no thread passed through.
levels.1: A few stitches are made, but they are long and uneven or the thread slips out of the cloth.
levels.2: A line of stitches runs along the dots, each about the same length, with thread showing on both sides.
levels.3: A curved line drawn by the child is sewn in stitches of the same size and the child names the over-and-under pattern.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name; dotted cloth is assumed. Cell gave only the step name.

rows.name: Reading and talking about the rhyme 'Counting in the Caribbean'
steps: Suggested: Read 'Counting in the Caribbean' aloud while children listen.
Suggested: Read it again and ask children to clap on each beat.
Suggested: Write the poem on the board and ask children to find words that sound alike at the line ends.
Suggested: Underline each rhyming pair in a different colour.
Suggested: Ask pairs to say another word that rhymes with one of the pairs.

levels.0: Poem on the board has no rhyming word underlined or named by the children.
levels.1: One rhyming pair from the poem is named, with help, while other pairs are missed.
levels.2: Rhyming words in 'Counting in the Caribbean' are named, such as the matching line endings, and the beat is clapped.
levels.3: A second poem, never read before, has its rhyming pair named and its beat clapped.

rows.note: Rubric follows the reviewer's corrected levels. Steps built from the poem name and unit.

rows.name: Making my own poem
steps: Suggested: Read two short rhyming chants and ask children to say which words rhyme.
Suggested: Choose a topic as a class, such as the school bus.
Suggested: Write a rhyming pair on the board and make the first two lines together.
Suggested: Ask children to write their own two or four lines in their notebooks, ending lines with a rhyming pair.
Suggested: Invite a few children to read their chant aloud.

levels.0: Notebook pages hold no chant lines, only the topic word.
levels.1: Lines of a chant are written, but the line endings do not rhyme, such as bus and tree.
levels.2: A short chant of two or more lines has rhyming words at the end of each line, such as bat and cat.
levels.3: A chant on a topic of the child's own choice has rhymes at all line ends, and the rhyming words are pointed out.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Words that sound the same but are spelt differently
steps: Suggested: Say 'sea' and 'see' aloud and ask what children notice about the sounds.
Suggested: Write both words on the board and talk about what each means.
Suggested: Show picture cards for pairs such as sun and son, two and to, and ask children to match the pairs.
Suggested: Have each child write two pairs in their notebooks.
Suggested: Ask each child to use one word in a spoken sentence.

levels.0: A written pair of same-sound words is missing from the notebook page.
levels.1: One pair, such as sun and son, is given, with a letter wrong in one of the words.
levels.2: Two pairs, such as sea and see, are given and each word is spelled correctly.
levels.3: Each word of a pair, such as to and two, is used in a sentence that fits its meaning.

rows.note: Rubric follows the reviewer's levels. Steps built from the activity name and unit.

rows.name: Measuring length: clips, strings, ruler and a measurement race
steps: Measure desks with paper clips and strings.
Guess the length first, then measure with a ruler.
Beginners estimate only; advanced children convert to centimetres.
Race: find 5 objects longer than your pencil.

levels.0: Measuring chart has no length filled in, and no object has been measured.
levels.1: Hand span counts are written, but the spans overlap or leave gaps along the edge.
levels.2: Each object is measured end to end in hand spans, with no gap, and its count is written.
levels.3: The same object measured with a pencil instead of a hand span is given a new count, and the child says why the two counts differ.

rows.name: Counting in multiples of 5 and 10
steps: Suggested: Make a number track from 0 to 100 on the floor or board.
Suggested: Clap and count aloud in fives, from 0, and mark each count on the track.
Suggested: Do the same in tens, from 0, and mark them in a different colour.
Suggested: Ask children to write the counted numbers in their notebooks in a row.
Suggested: Ask children what they notice about the last digit of the numbers.

levels.0: Counting by fives and tens is not attempted, and the notebook row stays empty.
levels.1: Fives are counted aloud from 0 to 25, then the count breaks off or slips to 26.
levels.2: Counting by fives and tens is said aloud from zero, with each number said in the right order up to 50 or more.
levels.3: The last digits 0 and 5 in a fives row are noticed and the child continues the count from a number the educator gives, such as 35.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name; the cell gave only the topic. Rubric is about skip counting aloud.

rows.name: Project 1: Snakes
steps: Suggested: Show pictures of snakes of different lengths and ask which is the longest.
Suggested: Give each child a length of string or wool to be a snake.
Suggested: Ask children to measure their snake in hand spans or paper clips and record the count.
Suggested: Colour or decorate the snake and display it with the measure beside it.
Suggested: Line up the snakes and say which is longest and which is shortest.

levels.0: Snake models have no measure written beside them.
levels.1: Snake lengths are counted in hand spans, but some spans are skipped or measured from the wrong end.
levels.2: Each snake is measured in hand spans or clips with no gaps, and its count is written next to it.
levels.3: Two snakes are measured with a unit the child chooses and ordered from longest to shortest, with the counts given as proof.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C17; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell names the project only. Materials (string, clips) are suggested. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!C16.

rows.name: Learning क to ङ consonants
steps: Suggested: Show the consonants क, ख, ग, घ, ङ on a chart and say each sound.
Suggested: Trace each letter in the air with a finger while saying it.
Suggested: Write each letter on the board with its starting point and direction.
Suggested: Ask children to copy each letter three times in their notebooks.
Suggested: Check formation and ask children to read each letter back.

levels.0: Notebook lines for क to ङ have no letter written at all.
levels.1: Letters क to ङ are copied, but ख and घ show a broken or backward shape.
levels.2: Each letter from क to ङ is copied with its correct shape and the shirorekha on the line.
levels.3: The same consonants, written from the educator's saying them aloud, hold their shape without the chart.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the letter range.

rows.name: Naming animals and birds
steps: Suggested: Show picture cards of animals and birds, such as गाय, शेर, तोता and मोर.
Suggested: Say each name and ask children to repeat it in Hindi.
Suggested: Hold up a card and ask 'यह क्या है?' for children to answer in Hindi.
Suggested: Place the cards into a mixed pile and let each pair name five of them.
Suggested: Ask children to say one animal and one bird they like.

levels.0: Picture cards of animals and birds draw no Hindi name from the child.
levels.1: A few cards get a Hindi name, but others are named in English, such as cow or parrot.
levels.2: Five or more animals and birds in the pictures are named in Hindi, each matching its card.
levels.3: Animal and bird names are sorted into two groups, पशु and पक्षी, and the sort is explained in a sentence.

rows.note: Rubric follows the reviewer's levels. Steps built from the unit पशु और पक्षी; picture cards are assumed.

rows.name: Reciting the 'Alphabet Chant'
steps: Suggested: Read the 'Alphabet Chant' by Rosemary Licciardi aloud while children listen.
Suggested: Read it again and let children clap the beat.
Suggested: Teach it one stanza at a time, with children repeating each line.
Suggested: Say the full chant together twice, with the page covered on the second time.
Suggested: Ask children to say the chant in pairs and then in front of the class.

levels.0: Alphabet Chant lines are not said when the page is covered.
levels.1: Some lines of the Alphabet Chant are said from memory, but later letters are skipped.
levels.2: Alphabet Chant is said from memory with its beat clapped, from the first letter to the last.
levels.3: A second chant, learnt this week, is said from memory with its rhythm kept, and the child says how the beat goes.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B21; steps are suggested from the activity name. Recite step is from the unit's speaking line.

rows.name: 'An Animal Rhyme' from Australia
steps: Suggested: Read 'An Animal Rhyme' from Australia aloud while children follow the text.
Suggested: Read it again and ask children to listen for words that sound alike.
Suggested: Write the rhyme on the board and circle the words that rhyme.
Suggested: Ask children to say a new word that rhymes with one of the pairs.
Suggested: Choose an animal from the rhyme and ask children to act it out.

levels.0: The animal rhyme is read, and no rhyming word is named by the children.
levels.1: One pair of rhyming words is named from the rhyme, with the rest left out.
levels.2: Rhyming words in 'An Animal Rhyme' are named, each pair matching the line endings.
levels.3: Another rhyme from a new country is read and its rhyming pair is named.

rows.note: Steps built from the poem name and unit; cell lists the topic only.

rows.name: Halves, quarters and symmetry painting
steps: Cut paper circles and squares into halves and quarters.
Cut an apple or orange into halves and quarters.
Fold paper, add paint on one side, press: a symmetry painting.
Use a mirror to check symmetry in letters and numbers.
rows.materials: Paper circles/squares, scissors, mirrors, paint, fruit

levels.0: Paper circles stay unfolded and no part is named.
levels.1: A half is named for a circle cut in two, but quarter and third are mixed up.
levels.2: Pizza halves, quarters and thirds are named correctly when shown a shape cut into equal parts.
levels.3: A new shape, such as a rectangle, is folded into equal parts and named, with a reason why unequal parts do not count.

rows.name: Revising च to ञ and calligraphy practice
steps: Suggested: Show the consonants च, छ, ज, झ, ञ on a chart and say each sound.
Suggested: Trace each letter in the air with a finger while saying it.
Suggested: Give each child the सुलेख माला and ask them to copy each letter on the lines.
Suggested: Move around and show children where each letter starts and ends.
Suggested: Ask children to read their letters aloud to a partner.

levels.0: सुलेख माला lines for च to ञ remain blank.
levels.1: Letters च to ञ are copied, though ज or झ lose a curve or sit below the line.
levels.2: Each letter from च to ञ is copied with the correct shape, resting on the shirorekha.
levels.3: Letters from च to ञ are written from dictation in a notebook with the shape held, and one child corrects a partner's letter.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; calligraphy book named in the cell.

rows.name: Listen, sing and tell a balgeet
steps: Suggested: Play or sing the balgeet twice while children listen.
Suggested: Teach the balgeet one line at a time, with children repeating each line.
Suggested: Sing the full balgeet together with a simple action for each line.
Suggested: Ask pairs to sing it to each other.
Suggested: Ask a few children to tell in a sentence what the balgeet is about.

levels.0: Balgeet lines are not sung by the child and the group song is met with silence.
levels.1: First lines of the balgeet are sung, with later words missed or hummed.
levels.2: The balgeet is sung from first line to last with the right words.
levels.3: After singing, the balgeet's subject is told in a sentence and one action is explained.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D21; steps are suggested from the activity name. Rubric follows the reviewer's levels. The balgeet is not named in the cell.

rows.name: Sorting materials
steps: Suggested: Gather a tray of objects such as a wooden spoon, a leaf, a plastic cup, a stone and a metal key.
Suggested: Place two sorting hoops labelled natural and made.
Suggested: Ask each child to pick one object and say where it goes.
Suggested: Talk about why the leaf and the stone go in one hoop and the cup and key in the other.
Suggested: Ask children to draw one object from each hoop in their notebooks.

levels.0: Sorting hoops are left empty, with no object placed.
levels.1: Objects such as a leaf and a stone go in the natural hoop, but a wooden spoon is also placed there.
levels.2: Each classroom object sits in the right hoop, natural or made, and the child names one object from each.
levels.3: A new object, such as a woollen sock, is placed in the right hoop and the choice is explained.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name; objects are suggested and not in the cell.

rows.name: Gandhi Jayanti skit
steps: Suggested: Show a picture of Gandhi ji and ask who children think he is.
Suggested: Tell a short story of Gandhi ji's life and his idea of truth and peace.
Suggested: Assign roles for a short skit: Gandhi ji, a child, a friend, a narrator.
Suggested: Rehearse the skit with simple lines and props such as a stick and glasses.
Suggested: Perform for the class, then ask children to name the leader they played.

levels.0: Gandhi ji's picture draws no name from the child.
levels.1: A leader of India is named as Gandhi ji only after the educator gives the first sound.
levels.2: When a picture is shown, Gandhi ji is named as a leader of India and one fact from the skit is said.
levels.3: A different leader, such as Nehru or Ambedkar, is named from a new picture and one thing about them is said.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G21; steps are suggested from the activity name. Skit is named in the cell; the skit's steps are built from the name and unit.

rows.name: Navratri: performing Garba and Dandiya
steps: Suggested: Show pictures of Garba and Dandiya and ask children what they notice.
Suggested: Tell the story of the nine days of Navratri in a few sentences.
Suggested: Teach the Garba clap pattern and the Dandiya stick pattern with a partner.
Suggested: Play music and let children practise in a circle.
Suggested: Perform for Navratri and ask children to say how it was celebrated.

levels.0: Pictures of Navratri bring no words about how the festival is celebrated.
levels.1: Garba is named from a picture, but Dandiya is not told apart from it.
levels.2: Garba or Dandiya is named from a picture and one way the festival is celebrated, such as dancing in a circle, is told.
levels.3: Another festival picture, such as Diwali, is named and its way of celebration is told in a full sentence.

rows.note: LO link is an assumption from the unit; steps built from the cell and common practice.

rows.name: Making an origami cup
steps: Suggested: Show the paper folding symbols, a dashed line for valley fold and a dot-dash line for mountain fold.
Suggested: Fold a square of paper into a valley fold and a mountain fold to practise.
Suggested: Follow the cup instructions step by step, folding over and over.
Suggested: Cut and make a stairstep fold as the cell lists.
Suggested: Check that the cup stands up and can hold a small object.

levels.0: Square paper stays flat and no origami cup is formed.
levels.1: Folds are made, but the corners do not meet and the cup falls over.
levels.2: An origami cup stands up with crisp valley and mountain folds and matching corners.
levels.3: A new origami shape, such as a boat or a hat, is made from paper without the educator showing every step.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!H21; steps are suggested from the activity name. Repeated in Mar H38.

rows.name: Hand sewing: needle stitches continued
steps: Suggested: Show a video of simple hand stitches.
Suggested: Hand each child cloth, needle and thread.
Suggested: Ask children to thread the needle and tie a knot.
Suggested: Ask children to sew a line of stitches along a marked line.
Suggested: Check each line with the child and point out one thing done well.

levels.0: Cloth stays free of stitches, and the thread is not passed through.
levels.1: Stitches are made but are uneven in length or thread loops loosely on top.
levels.2: A row of running stitches, each about the same size, runs along the marked line on the cloth.
levels.3: A longer line with a turn, stitched without a marked guide, keeps the stitch size and the child explains how to stop with a knot.

rows.note: Video link in materials is the educators' own reference. Steps built from the activity name and unit.

rows.name: Making my own poem and reciting it to the school
steps: Suggested: Choose a topic as a class and make two rhyming lines together.
Suggested: Ask each child to write their own four lines in their notebooks, ending lines with rhyming words.
Suggested: Pair children to read poems to each other and fix any word that does not rhyme.
Suggested: Practise saying the poem from memory three times.
Suggested: Invite children to recite their poem at the school assembly.

levels.0: Notebook pages hold no poem lines, and the school recitation is not attempted.
levels.1: A poem is written with some rhymes, but when recited the lines are read from the page with the beat lost.
levels.2: The poem has rhyming words at the end of its lines and is recited from memory with a steady rhythm.
levels.3: A poem recited to the school is delivered with a clear voice, and the rhyming pairs are named when asked.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B22; steps are suggested from the activity name. Two LOs linked; rubric covers the first (writing the rhyming chant) with the recitation as the extension.

rows.name: Rhymes from China and Japan
steps: Suggested: Read 'A lullaby from China' aloud and ask children to sway to the rhythm.
Suggested: Read 'A kite rhyme from Japan' aloud and ask children to listen for words that sound alike.
Suggested: Write both rhymes on the board and circle the rhyming words in each.
Suggested: Ask pairs to say one new word that rhymes with a circled word.
Suggested: Talk about how the two rhymes are the same and how they are different.

levels.0: The two rhymes are read, but no rhyming word from either is named.
levels.1: A rhyming pair is found in the lullaby, but none is found in the kite rhyme.
levels.2: The lullaby and the kite rhyme each have their rhyming words named, matching the line endings.
levels.3: A third rhyme from a new country is read and the rhyming pair is named at once.

rows.note: Steps built from the rhyme titles and unit.

rows.name: Revising ट to न and calligraphy practice
steps: Suggested: Show the consonants ट, ठ, ड, ढ, ण, त, थ, द, ध, न on a chart and say each sound.
Suggested: Trace each letter in the air with a finger while saying it.
Suggested: Give each child the सुलेख माला and ask them to copy each letter on the lines.
Suggested: Check that each letter hangs from the shirorekha.
Suggested: Ask children to read their letters aloud to a partner.

levels.0: सुलेख माला lines for ट to न remain empty.
levels.1: Letters ट to न are copied, but ड and ढ are mixed up or their dots are missing.
levels.2: Each letter from ट to न is copied with the right shape, hanging from the shirorekha.
levels.3: Letters ट to न written from dictation keep their shape, and a look-alike pair such as ड and ढ is told apart aloud.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; calligraphy book named in the cell.

rows.name: How to start a conversation
steps: Suggested: Role-play two children meeting on the first day and ask what the first one says.
Suggested: Teach opening lines for a conversation: नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं?, आपका नाम क्या है?.
Suggested: Have pairs practise the opening lines with each other.
Suggested: Add one question to keep the talk going, such as 'आप कहाँ रहते हैं?'.
Suggested: Ask a few pairs to show their conversation to the class.

levels.0: No Hindi opening line is said to the partner.
levels.1: नमस्ते is said, but the next line comes only after the educator prompts it.
levels.2: A short Hindi exchange is held with नमस्ते, a question such as आपका नाम क्या है? and a reply.
levels.3: An extra question such as आप कहाँ रहते हैं? keeps the talk going with a new partner.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D22; steps are suggested from the activity name. Rubric follows the reviewer's levels. Reviewer noted the linked LO (G1-NEW-003: speaking on a topic) covers talking, not starting; please confirm. Character/wellbeing activity: no graded levels (ADR 0037); look-fors instead. Graded levels replace the earlier look-fors (reviewer round 4).

rows.name: Reading, word meaning and questions: The Ungrateful Tiger; Tiddalik and the thirsty frog
steps: Suggested: Read 'The Ungrateful Tiger' aloud and ask children to listen for who is in the story.
Suggested: Ask children to name the characters and say one thing each did.
Suggested: Read 'Tiddalik and the thirsty frog' and ask the same.
Suggested: Pick three new words from each tale and talk about what they mean.
Suggested: Ask children what each tale teaches.

levels.0: Tale characters are not named and the questions about the story are not answered.
levels.1: Tiger is named from the first tale, but the second tale's frog is missed.
levels.2: The main characters of both tales, such as the tiger and Tiddalik, are named after reading.
levels.3: Characters from a new traditional tale, told only once, are named and the lesson is said in a sentence.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B27; steps are suggested from the activity name. Two LOs linked; rubric is about the first (naming the characters). Lesson is the second LO.

rows.name: Adjacent consonants practice
steps: Suggested: Write the words 'jump', 'frog', 'splash' and 'strip' on cards.
Suggested: Read each card aloud, sounding out each letter, and ask children to repeat.
Suggested: Sort the cards into CVCC, CCVC and CCVCC groups.
Suggested: Give each pair a set of word cards and ask them to read each one.
Suggested: Ask children to write one word from each group on their slate.

levels.0: Word cards with two or three consonants together are left unread.
levels.1: Words such as jump are read, but frog and strip lose a consonant or are read with an extra vowel.
levels.2: Each CCVC and CVCC card, such as frog or jump, is read aloud with every consonant sounded.
levels.3: A new card, such as 'crisp' or 'stamp', is read at once and the child says how many sounds it has.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the shapes the cell lists; words are suggested.

rows.name: Tricky words practice
steps: Suggested: Hold up a flash card for each of the words in the cell and read it aloud.
Suggested: Ask children to repeat each word, then read it without help.
Suggested: Mix the cards and play a game where a child picks a card and reads it.
Suggested: Pair the cards into the two lists from the cell and read the first list.
Suggested: Read the second list, then ask children to find any word in a sentence on the board.

levels.0: Flash cards for like, come, some and were are not read.
levels.1: Like and come are read on sight, but were, there and little are sounded out wrongly.
levels.2: All eleven tricky words (like, come, some, were, there, little, one, do, when, out, what) are read aloud on sight from the cards.
levels.3: Tricky words such as when and what are found and read in a new sentence on the board.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!B27; steps are suggested from the activity name. Two LOs linked; rubric is about the first (the 11 words like, come, some, were, there, little, one, do, when, out, what).

rows.name: Reading polysyllabic words
steps: Suggested: Write words such as 'rabbit', 'sunset' and 'elephant' in syllable chunks on cards.
Suggested: Clap the beats of each word and ask children to count the claps.
Suggested: Read each word one chunk at a time, then say it whole.
Suggested: Give pairs a word list to read and clap together.
Suggested: Ask children to circle each chunk in their notebooks.

levels.0: Word lists with two- and three-syllable words go unread.
levels.1: Two-syllable words such as rabbit are read, but longer words are read as one chunk or lose a syllable.
levels.2: Words of two or three syllables from the list are read aloud, each chunk said in turn and then blended.
levels.3: New words such as 'umbrella' are read in chunks and the number of syllables is clapped correctly.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell lists the topic only. Words are suggested.

rows.name: Addition of single digits with pictures and the number line
steps: Suggested: Show a picture of three birds and two more arriving and ask how many in all.
Suggested: Write the sum horizontally as 3 + 2 = 5.
Suggested: Use a number line to start at 3 and jump 2 to land on 5.
Suggested: Write the same sum vertically with a line underneath.
Suggested: Give each pair five picture cards and ask them to add and write each sum both ways.

levels.0: Picture cards are left without a sum written for them.
levels.1: Sums are written for the picture clues, but several answers are off by one.
levels.2: Sums within 20 are written correctly from a picture clue and from a jump on the number line.
levels.3: A new pair of numbers is added in both horizontal and vertical forms, and a missing number is found by working back.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!C27; steps are suggested from the activity name. Two LOs linked; rubric is about the first (recall of addition facts within 20).

rows.name: 2-digit addition with and without regrouping
steps: Suggested: Show 24 + 3 with tens rods and ones cubes and say the sum aloud.
Suggested: Write 24 + 3 in the notebook, adding the ones then the tens.
Suggested: Show 27 + 15 with blocks and exchange ten ones for one ten rod.
Suggested: Write the sum with the regrouped ten shown above the tens column.
Suggested: Give each pair five sums, some with and some without regrouping, to solve and check.

levels.0: Notebook sums in the addition exercise are left without any answer written.
levels.1: Sums such as 24 + 3 are right, but with 27 + 15 the ones digit is written twice or the ten is lost.
levels.2: Sums with and without regrouping, such as 27 + 15 = 42, are right on paper, with the regrouped ten shown.
levels.3: The regrouped ten is shown with blocks or in the place-value chart, and the child says why the ten moves to the tens column.
