rows.note: Cell C27 says 'with carry'; school wording is regroup/exchange. Steps are suggested.

rows.name: Word problems on addition
steps: Suggested: Read a story such as 'There are 4 birds on a tree and 3 more come' and ask children to draw it.
Suggested: Ask how many birds there are in all and write the number sentence.
Suggested: Give each pair counters to act out a second story, with 8 sweets and 3 eaten.
Suggested: Ask children to solve three more word problems with drawings or counters.
Suggested: Ask a few children to tell how they found the answer.

levels.0: Word problem sheets are left with no drawing, counters or answer.
levels.1: Drawings of the objects are made, but the answer is wrong because the wrong operation is used.
levels.2: Drawings or counters show the story, and the written answer to the one-step problem is right.
levels.3: Another word problem, with the other operation, is solved and the child tells the story in their own words.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Cayley's table
steps: Suggested: Draw a Cayley's table grid on the board with the numbers 0 to 5 along the top and side.
Suggested: Show how to fill the first cell by adding the row number and column number.
Suggested: Fill the first row together and ask children what they notice.
Suggested: Give each child a grid and ask them to fill in the rest.
Suggested: Ask children to colour any repeated numbers in the same colour.

levels.0: Cayley's table grids are handed in with cells left empty.
levels.1: Cells in the first rows are filled in, but the sums later in the grid are wrong.
levels.2: Every cell in Cayley's table holds the correct sum of its row and column numbers.
levels.3: A repeating diagonal in the table is spotted and a new, larger table is completed from the same rule.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell names it only.

rows.name: Comparing numbers 10 to 99 with <, > and =
steps: Suggested: Write two numbers on the board, such as 34 and 43, and ask which is greater.
Suggested: Teach that the open side of < and > faces the larger number.
Suggested: Ask children to write a sign between pairs of numbers on their slates.
Suggested: Give each pair a set of number cards to compare and write down.
Suggested: Ask children to explain one comparison, using the tens digit first.

levels.0: Slates have no sign written between the two numbers.
levels.1: Both signs < and > appear, but some are turned the wrong way round.
levels.2: Both signs < and > face the greater number, and = is used when the numbers match, with all comparisons from 10 to 99 right.
levels.3: A hidden sign is placed between two numbers and the child says that the tens digit is checked first.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name; cell gave the signs and the range.

rows.name: Reading words without matras and words with the आ matra
steps: Suggested: Show word cards without matras, such as कमल and घर, and read them aloud.
Suggested: Introduce the आ matra with words like काम, नाम and आम.
Suggested: Ask children to read each word in chunks, first the letters then the matra.
Suggested: Show picture cards and ask children to pick the word with the correct matra.
Suggested: Ask children to write the missing matra in a word under a picture.

levels.0: Cards showing pictures stay unmatched to words, and no matra is written.
levels.1: Words without a matra are matched to pictures, but the आ matra is left off or put in the wrong place.
levels.2: The correct matra, such as आ in काम, is picked to finish a word shown with a picture.
levels.3: A new picture word, with the आ matra, is completed and the child says which letter the matra sits on.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit.

rows.name: New poem 'बतूता का जूता' and recitation
steps: Suggested: Read the poem 'बतूता का जूता' aloud while children follow the text.
Suggested: Read it again with actions for the shoe and the walking.
Suggested: Teach the poem one line at a time, with children repeating each line.
Suggested: Recite the full poem together, then in pairs.
Suggested: Ask a few children to recite it alone.

levels.0: Silence follows when the group begins the poem, and no line is recited.
levels.1: Opening lines of 'बतूता का जूता' are recited, with several words missed or changed.
levels.2: 'बतूता का जूता' is recited in full with each word right.
levels.3: 'बतूता का जूता' is recited alone in front of the class with the actions for the shoe and the walking, with no prompt.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D27; steps are suggested from the activity name. Rubric follows the reviewer's levels. Reviewer noted the cell mixes three things (new poem, revision, topic talk); steps keep the new poem as the main line.

rows.name: Green Day: walk to school
steps: Suggested: Talk with children about why cars make smoke and what emissions do to the air.
Suggested: Introduce AQI with a simple chart of green, yellow and red.
Suggested: Ask children to walk to school on Green Day, with parents in the lead.
Suggested: On return, ask each child what they saw and how the air felt.
Suggested: Ask children to name one way to look after the air, such as walking or using the bus.

levels.0: No way to look after the environment is named in the class talk.
levels.1: Looking after the environment is named in a general way, such as 'keep it clean', with no specific way given.
levels.2: One specific way to look after the environment, such as saving water or walking to school, is named in the class talk.
levels.3: Two ways are named, with a reason, in a talk about a new place such as the park or the river.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G27; steps are suggested from the activity name. Linked to the 'looks after the environment' LO. Walk is run by families; educator checks plans and safety.

rows.name: Christmas Carnival: jingle and display
steps: Suggested: Choose a short jingle with four lines and teach it one line at a time.
Suggested: Add one action for each line, such as clapping, jingling bells or swaying.
Suggested: Practise the jingle in groups, with each group taking one line.
Suggested: Make a Christmas display with paper stars and trees on the wall.
Suggested: Perform the jingle for another class beside the display.

levels.0: Jingle lines are not sung and no action is made.
levels.1: The jingle is sung, but the actions come after the words or are missed on some lines.
levels.2: Jingle words and actions match in time, with the child and group finishing together.
levels.3: A new line or verse is learnt, and its action is made at the same moment as the word.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!G27; steps are suggested from the activity name. Reviewer flagged leading groups as beyond Grade 1; steps use group jingle and a simple class display instead. LO link is an assumption.

rows.name: Hand sewing: Christmas craft
steps: Suggested: Show a finished felt Christmas craft, such as a star or a tree.
Suggested: Give each child two pieces of felt with the shape marked on them.
Suggested: Ask children to thread the needle and sew around the edge with running stitches.
Suggested: Stuff the shape lightly and finish with a knot.
Suggested: Ask children to hold up the craft and name the stitch they used.

levels.0: Felt pieces for the Christmas craft are left unstitched.
levels.1: A few stitches hold the felt, but gaps appear between them along the edge.
levels.2: A line of running stitches along the Christmas craft's edge holds the two pieces together with even spacing.
levels.3: A second shape of the child's own design is sewn along its edge and the stitch name is said.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic. Felt and the craft shape are suggested.

rows.name: Design Lab project: The Earth – Globe
steps: Suggested: Show a globe and ask children what colours they see for land and sea.
Suggested: Give each child a round balloon or ball of papier-mache layers.
Suggested: Paint the sea blue and the land green or brown.
Suggested: Ask children to point to India on the globe.
Suggested: Display the globes and ask children to say what they made.

levels.0: Globe models are not made, and the materials stay unused.
levels.1: A round shape is made, but the paint shows no land or sea.
levels.2: The globe shows land and sea in different colours and is round.
levels.3: India and one ocean are labelled on the globe and pointed out when asked.

rows.note: Rubric follows the reviewer's levels. Steps built from the activity name; the cell names no plan, so the LO's 'plan' is the picture of a globe.

rows.name: Making my own traditional tale
steps: Suggested: Read the opening line of a traditional tale, such as 'Once upon a time', and ask what comes next.
Suggested: Talk about how a tale starts, has a problem and ends.
Suggested: Choose a character and a problem together, such as a clever hare and a river.
Suggested: Ask children to write a start and an ending in two sentences.
Suggested: Ask a few children to read their tale to the class.

levels.0: Notebooks have no tale lines, only a character name or a drawing.
levels.1: A tale starts with 'Once upon a time', but the ending is left or copied from a known tale.
levels.2: A different ending for a traditional tale is written in one or two sentences, and it fits the problem.
levels.3: A new ending is written for a second tale and the child tells why it changes the lesson.

levels.1: Sentences are written but they do not follow the order of the pictures.
levels.2: One sentence per picture follows the picture sequence in order.
levels.3: An ending that is not shown in the pictures is added to the story in a new sentence.

rows.note: LO link or content is an assumption from the unit and siblings. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Venn and Carroll diagrams, pictograms and block graphs
steps: Sort fruits sweet/sour in a Venn diagram.
Classify animals, shapes or colours in a Carroll diagram.
Survey favourite fruits or toys.
Show the survey in a pictogram and a block graph.

levels.0: Charts made in class are left with no question answered about them.
levels.1: A chart is read for one box or bar but the other boxes are not read.
levels.2: What the Carroll diagram or graph shows is told aloud using counts from each box or bar.
levels.3: A new chart is made from fresh data and a question is answered from it.

rows.name: Sorting coins and banknotes by value
steps: Suggested: Show real or toy coins and notes of India.
Suggested: Read the value written on each coin and note aloud.
Suggested: Ask children to sort the coins and notes into groups by value.
Suggested: Order the groups from smallest to largest value.
Suggested: Ask each pair to name the coins in their group.

levels.0: Coins and notes sit in one heap and none is named by its value.
levels.1: Some coins are named but notes are confused with coins of other values.
levels.2: Coins and notes of India are named by the value written on them and grouped by value.
levels.3: A mixed pile is sorted into groups of equal value and the smallest and largest are named.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and materials.

rows.name: Words with ए, ऐ, ओ, औ matras
steps: Suggested: Practise writing letters on the सुलेख माला pages.
Suggested: Write words with ए, ऐ, ओ and औ on the board and read them.
Suggested: Show how the matras attach above the letter.
Suggested: Ask children to write each matra with a letter in a notebook.
Suggested: Show picture cards for children to complete with the correct matra.

levels.0: Words on the picture cards are finished without any matra.
levels.1: Matras are added but ए and ऐ or ओ and औ are mixed up.
levels.2: Picture words are completed with ए, ऐ, ओ or औ and are read correctly.
levels.3: A fresh word with ो or ौ is written correctly from dictation.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!D39; steps are suggested from the activity name.

rows.name: Dictation of sentences
steps: Suggested: Say a short Hindi sentence aloud and ask children to repeat it.
Suggested: Break the sentence into words and say each word slowly.
Suggested: Have children write the sentence in a notebook.
Suggested: Read it aloud again so children can check their work.
Suggested: Compare each sentence with the board and fix matras.

levels.0: Dictation page has no written word from the sentence.
levels.1: Words from the sentence are written but matras are left out or wrong.
levels.2: The dictated sentence is written with the right matras and spaces between words.
levels.3: A sentence with a word not heard before is written correctly from dictation.

rows.note: LO link or content is an assumption from the unit and siblings. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Project 1 – Place Value City
steps: Suggested: Show cards for hundreds, tens and ones with number cards.
Suggested: Pick a three-digit number and show its hundreds, tens and ones.
Suggested: Have each group build a tall, medium and small building for each place.
Suggested: Place the buildings in a city and label them with number cards.
Suggested: Read the city's number aloud.

levels.0: City layout has no building cards linked to a number.
levels.1: Buildings are built but hundreds, tens and ones buildings are not told apart.
levels.2: A city is built where tall, middle and short buildings show hundreds, tens and ones for a number.
levels.3: A new number is built into the city and its place value parts are said aloud.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D33; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus line gives the project in one sentence; steps are built from it.

rows.name: Project 2 – Money Market
steps: Suggested: Set up a small classroom shop with priced items.
Suggested: Give each child play money in coins and notes.
Suggested: Take turns being the shopkeeper and the buyer.
Suggested: Count the money and give back change.
Suggested: Record one purchase on a bill.

levels.0: Shop items change hands with no play money counted out.
levels.1: Play money is handed over but the amount does not match the price.
levels.2: Items are bought with play money that matches the price shown.
levels.3: A purchase is paid for with a different mix of coins and the change is counted back.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D33; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus line gives the project in one sentence; steps are built from it.

rows.name: Project 3 – Fraction Pizza Shop
steps: Suggested: Give each child a paper circle to be a pizza.
Suggested: Fold and cut one pizza into two equal halves.
Suggested: Fold and cut another pizza into three and four equal parts.
Suggested: Label each piece as half, third or quarter.
Suggested: Compare the size of the pieces.

levels.0: Paper pizzas stay whole with no cut or fold made.
levels.1: Pizzas are cut into parts but the pieces are not equal in size.
levels.2: A paper pizza is cut into equal halves, thirds or quarters and each part is named.
levels.3: Halves of a pizza are cut again into quarters and the link between them is explained.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D33; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus line gives the project in one sentence; steps are built from it.

rows.name: Project 4 – Measure the Garden
steps: Suggested: Take children around the classroom and garden to choose objects and plants to measure.
Suggested: Show how to measure with hand spans and footsteps.
Suggested: Measure each object with the same hand or step each time.
Suggested: Record the counts in a table.
Suggested: Compare which was longest and shortest.

levels.0: Table of measures has no count written for any object.
levels.1: An object is measured but hand spans or steps overlap or leave gaps.
levels.2: Plants and objects are measured with hands or steps and the count is recorded.
levels.3: Two measured objects are compared and the longer one is named.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D33; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus line gives the project in one sentence; steps are built from it.

rows.name: Project 5 – Pattern Parade
steps: Suggested: Collect beads, tiles, leaves and pieces of cloth to show patterns.
Suggested: Look at the patterns and say the repeating part.
Suggested: Lay out a pattern with the items on a mat.
Suggested: Ask a partner to add the next three items.
Suggested: Display the patterns in a parade.

levels.0: Collected items are not laid out in any repeating order.
levels.1: A pattern starts but items added after the repeat break the pattern.
levels.2: A pattern of beads, tiles or leaves is extended by adding the next items correctly.
levels.3: A new pattern is made and its repeating unit is named aloud.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D33; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus line gives the project in one sentence; steps are built from it.

rows.name: Project 6 – Time Detectives
steps: Suggested: Make a timeline strip with morning, afternoon and evening.
Suggested: Show picture cards of school routines such as assembly, snack and lunch.
Suggested: Place the cards in the order they happen.
Suggested: Add the clock time to each card.
Suggested: Check the order with a partner.

levels.0: Timeline strip stays empty with no routine card placed on it.
levels.1: Some cards are placed but their order does not match the school day.
levels.2: Routine and event cards are placed in order on the timeline.
levels.3: A new event is added in its right place and the time is read from a clock.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D33; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus line gives the project in one sentence; steps are built from it.

rows.name: Amazing Seeds
steps: Suggested: Give each pair a few seeds of different kinds.
Suggested: Look at the seeds with a hand lens.
Suggested: Say how the seeds differ in size, shape and colour.
Suggested: Draw two seeds side by side.
Suggested: Plant a seed in a cup and watch for growth.

levels.0: Seeds are looked at but no difference between them is told.
levels.1: Two seeds are named but their difference is not described.
levels.2: Two seeds are described by size, shape or colour differences seen up close.
levels.3: A seed is described and a guess is made about the plant it will grow into.

rows.note: LO link or content is an assumption from the unit and siblings. Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: What Melts What?
steps: Suggested: Show materials such as wax, chocolate, ice and clay.
Suggested: Guess which will melt when warmed.
Suggested: Warm each material safely in sunlight or warm water.
Suggested: Watch and note what changes.
Suggested: Sort the materials into melts and does not melt.

levels.0: Materials are warmed but no change is told afterwards.
levels.1: A change is seen in one material but the others are not checked.
levels.2: What happened to each material when warmed is told and sorted into melts and does not melt.
levels.3: A new material is guessed to melt or not and then tested.

rows.note: Syllabus names the project only. Steps built from the activity name. LO title is about bending and squashing; heat effect is the focus here (check LO-G1-0137).

rows.name: Water Watchers
steps: Suggested: Fill a tub with water and collect small objects.
Suggested: Guess if each object floats or sinks.
Suggested: Place each object in the water and watch.
Suggested: Sort the objects on a float and sink chart.
Suggested: Say why some objects float.

levels.0: Float and sink chart stays empty of results.
levels.1: Objects are tested but the same job or test is not used for each one.
levels.2: Objects are tested the same way in water and sorted into float and sink.
levels.3: A new object is guessed and tested, and the reason for the result is told.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and materials. LO title is about testing materials for a job; float and sink fits only partly (check LO-G1-0136).

rows.name: Light & Shadow Play
steps: Suggested: Give each pair a torch, a lidded shoebox and two or three small objects.
Suggested: Shine the torch on an object and trace its shadow on paper.
Suggested: Move the torch closer and farther and watch how the shadow changes.
Suggested: Put the lid on the box and let each child peek in through a small hole.
Suggested: Ask each pair to say why it is dark inside the box.

levels.0: Nothing is said about why the covered box looks dark, and no shadow is traced.
levels.1: Shadows are traced on paper, yet the dark inside the box is called 'night' with no mention of light.
levels.2: Darkness inside the covered box is explained as 'no light gets in' after looking through the hole.
levels.3: A closed cupboard or drawer is explained as dark for the same reason, with the idea that an object blocks light to make a shadow.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic. Closest LO: darkness is where there is no light.

rows.name: Animal Homes
steps: Suggested: Lay out habitat mats for a forest, a pond, a desert and a farm.
Suggested: Give each child an animal picture card.
Suggested: Ask each child to say where the animal lives and place the card on that mat.
Suggested: Ask what the animal finds there, such as food, water or shelter.
Suggested: Look at any card placed on a different mat and talk about why it belongs elsewhere.

levels.0: Animal cards stay in the pile with none placed on a habitat mat.
levels.1: Fish and bird cards land on the wrong mat until the educator names the habitat aloud.
levels.2: Each animal card sits on the habitat mat where that animal lives, such as the fish on the pond mat.
levels.3: Camel and penguin cards not met in class go to the right mat with a reason such as 'it is hot and sandy'.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Senses Survey
steps: Suggested: Set up five stations: smell jars, tasting bits, a feely bag, a sound box and a picture to look at.
Suggested: Let each child try one item at every station.
Suggested: At each station ask which body part was used.
Suggested: Record each answer as a tally on a class chart of the five senses.
Suggested: Count which sense was used at the most stations.

levels.0: The survey chart has no sense named at any station.
levels.1: Seeing and hearing get the right names, but smelling and tasting are mixed up with each other.
levels.2: Smelling, tasting, touching, hearing and seeing are each named correctly right after trying the matching station.
levels.3: A sense is named for a fresh case such as hearing a bell or feeling a pillow, with the body part pointed to.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Spelling Bee (weekly)
steps: Suggested: Choose ten known words from the week's reading.
Suggested: Sit children in a circle and say one word clearly.
Suggested: Ask one child to say the word, spell it letter by letter, then say it again.
Suggested: Ask the class to show a thumbs up if every letter was right.
Suggested: Come back to missed words at the end of the round.

levels.0: No letters are spoken after the educator says the word.
levels.1: Letters are called out with one dropped or swapped, such as f-o-g for frog, until the educator repeats the word.
levels.2: Every letter of the given word is said in order, ending with the whole word.
levels.3: Letters come out in the right order for a word not yet practised, such as one from a new story.

rows.note: Syllabus gives the purpose only. Steps built from the activity name.

rows.name: Dictation (weekly)
steps: Suggested: Say five known words one at a time and ask children to write each.
Suggested: Read one short sentence slowly, then again in chunks.
Suggested: Ask children to write the sentence in their notebooks.
Suggested: Read it a final time so children check their own writing.
Suggested: Show the sentence on the board and ask children to tick or fix each word.

levels.0: No part of the dictated sentence is written.
levels.1: The sentence is written, but two or three words have missing or swapped letters.
levels.2: The dictated sentence is written with every word spelt correctly.
levels.3: A second, longer dictated sentence is written correctly with a capital letter and a full stop.

rows.note: Syllabus gives the purpose only. Steps built from the activity name; levels follow the reviewer's correction.

rows.name: Reading Project (weekly)
steps: Suggested: Set up a book corner with books at the right reading level.
Suggested: Let each child choose one book.
Suggested: Give ten minutes of silent reading.
Suggested: Ask each child to tell a partner one thing from the book.
Suggested: Write the book title in a reading log.

levels.0: The reading log has no title and the chosen book stays unopened during reading time.
levels.1: Pictures are looked at and pages turned, but words on the page are not read in order.
levels.2: A chosen book is read page by page through the whole reading time, with its title noted in the log.
levels.3: A second book from another type is chosen and read the next week, with one event or fact from it told to a partner.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D84; steps are suggested from the activity name. Syllabus gives the purpose only. Steps built from the activity name. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H4.

rows.name: Novel reading – the Nate the Great series (weekly)
steps: Suggested: Show the cover and read the first lines of the chapter aloud.
Suggested: Let children read the chapter alone, in pairs or in groups.
Suggested: Ask who was in the chapter and what happened.
Suggested: Ask children to say the beginning, middle and end to a partner.
Suggested: Invite two children to retell the chapter to the class.

levels.0: Nothing from the chapter is told after reading, and the questions get no answer.
levels.1: Names such as Nate or Sludge are said, but the events are out of order or the end is missing.
levels.2: The chapter's events are told in the order they happened, naming Nate and what he did.
levels.3: A chapter is retold with a guess about the next one, such as who Nate will ask next.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D88; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the Nate the Great series. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H11.

rows.name: Reading a picture story (चित्रकथा) and making a story on the pictures
steps: Suggested: Give each child a picture story (चित्रकथा) with few words.
Suggested: Look through all the pages together without talking.
Suggested: Ask children to say one Hindi sentence for each page.
Suggested: Ask pairs to tell the story to each other from first page to last.
Suggested: Invite two children to tell it to the class.

levels.0: No Hindi sentence is spoken for any page of the picture story.
levels.1: Single words naming things in the pictures, such as 'चिड़िया', are said without being joined into a story.
levels.2: A Hindi sentence is told for each page, in page order, so the pictures make one story.
levels.3: The story is told again with a new ending and a name for each character.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Writing a story on pictures (चित्रों पर कहानी लेखन)
steps: Suggested: Show three or four pictures in order on the board.
Suggested: Talk about who is there, where it is and what happens.
Suggested: Ask children to write one Hindi sentence under each picture.
Suggested: Ask them to add a title and an ending line.
Suggested: Ask each child to read the story to a partner.

levels.0: The page holds the pictures but no written Hindi sentence beneath them.
levels.1: A single word or label is written under each picture, with no full sentence joining them.
levels.2: One written Hindi sentence sits under each picture, and together they tell the story in order.
levels.3: A story from a fresh picture set has a beginning, a middle, an end and a title.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Letter writing practice (अक्षर लेखन अभ्यास)
steps: Suggested: Write one Hindi letter on the board and name its strokes.
Suggested: Ask children to trace it in the air and on their palms.
Suggested: Ask them to trace dotted copies of the letter.
Suggested: Ask them to write a row of the letter in the notebook, with the shirorekha.
Suggested: Ask pairs to swap notebooks and point to the best letter.

levels.0: No Hindi letter is written in the notebook line after the educator's model.
levels.1: Letters are formed with wrong strokes or in the wrong direction, such as the shirorekha missing.
levels.2: Letters sit on the line in the right shape, each with its shirorekha.
levels.3: Letters in a neat row is written neatly from memory, with the model covered.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; levels follow the reviewer's correction.

rows.name: Reading and singing the song 'चंदा मामा'
steps: Suggested: Write the song 'चंदा मामा' on a chart.
Suggested: Sing it once while children listen.
Suggested: Read it line by line together, pointing to each word.
Suggested: Sing line by line and ask children to repeat each line.
Suggested: Sing the whole song together, with a clap on the beat.

levels.0: Lips stay still and no line of the song is sung with the group.
levels.1: The tune is hummed and the first line is sung, but later lines are missed or words are changed.
levels.2: All lines of 'चंदा मामा' are sung with the tune, together with the group.
levels.3: The song is led from its first line without the educator, with actions added to the lines.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Matching letters to pictures and writing (अक्षर–चित्र मिलाकर लेखन)
steps: Suggested: Lay out picture cards and cards with letters and matras.
Suggested: Ask a child to pick a picture and say its name slowly.
Suggested: Ask the child to put the letter cards in order to build the word.
Suggested: Ask the child to write the word in the notebook.
Suggested: Check the word against the picture together.

levels.0: A picture card is picked but no letters are matched or written beside it.
levels.1: The first letter is written for the picture, but the matra or later letters are missing.
levels.2: The word for each picture is written with its letters and matras joined in the right order.
levels.3: A word for a picture not used before is written correctly, with a matra, and put into a sentence.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Rewriting the fish story (कहानी का पुनर्लेखन)
steps: Suggested: Read the fish story aloud to the class.
Suggested: Ask who was in it and what happened.
Suggested: Ask each child to tell the beginning, middle and end to a partner.
Suggested: Ask children to write the story in their own words in the notebook.
Suggested: Ask them to read it back and fix one thing.

levels.0: The notebook page has the title but no rewritten line from the fish story.
levels.1: Sentences copied straight from the book fill the page, with none changed into new words.
levels.2: The fish story is rewritten in own words and in order, from the beginning to the end.
levels.3: The story is rewritten with a changed ending or a new character, still in clear order.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Writing a poem (कविता लेखन)
steps: Suggested: Sing the song together and write its rhyming word pairs on the board.
Suggested: Ask children to list more words that sound alike.
Suggested: Give a two-line frame to start the poem.
Suggested: Ask children to write two to four lines that end in rhyming words.
Suggested: Ask each child to read the poem aloud.

levels.0: No poem lines appear and the list of song words is empty.
levels.1: Lines are written with song words, but the line endings do not rhyme.
levels.2: A short poem of two to four lines ends in rhyming words taken from the song.
levels.3: A rhyming poem is written about a new topic such as rain, with rhymes not found in the song.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Describing a picture and writing (चित्र वर्णन और लेखन)
steps: Suggested: Show a picture from the kitchen story.
Suggested: Ask what can be seen and what the people are doing.
Suggested: Ask children to say two or three sentences aloud.
Suggested: Ask them to write those sentences in Hindi.
Suggested: Ask each child to read the sentences to a partner.

levels.0: Beneath the kitchen picture the page stays blank.
levels.1: One-word labels such as 'चूल्हा' are written for things in the picture, with no sentence.
levels.2: Two or three Hindi sentences tell what is in the kitchen picture and what is happening.
levels.3: Sentences describe a different picture, such as a market, saying what people are doing and where.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Making two sentences from one word (शब्द से दो वाक्य बनाना)
steps: Suggested: Write a word with two meanings on the board, such as 'आम' or 'कल'.
Suggested: Say both meanings and draw a small picture for each.
Suggested: Ask children to say one sentence for each meaning.
Suggested: Ask them to write both sentences in the notebook.
Suggested: Invite a few children to read their pair of sentences.

levels.0: Neither sentence appears in the notebook for the given two-meaning word.
levels.1: One sentence is written with the word, but the second uses the same meaning again.
levels.2: Two written sentences each use the word in one of its two meanings.
levels.3: Two sentences are made for a second two-meaning word, with each meaning drawn or said.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Matching opposite words (शब्द–जोड़ी मिलान)
steps: Suggested: Make word cards with opposites, such as बड़ा and छोटा.
Suggested: Spread the cards face up on the floor.
Suggested: Ask each child to pick a card and find its opposite.
Suggested: Ask pairs to read their matched cards aloud.
Suggested: Turn the cards face down and play a memory pairs game.

levels.0: Cards stay unpaired and no word is joined to its opposite.
levels.1: Easy pairs such as बड़ा and छोटा are matched, while less familiar words stay left over.
levels.2: Every word card is paired with its opposite and each pair is read aloud.
levels.3: An opposite is said for a new word that is on no card.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: My Family picture-and-sentence mini book
steps: Suggested: Build 2–3 word sentences from known words.
Suggested: Make a mini book with a picture and a sentence on each page.
Suggested: Share the mini book with a partner by reading one page aloud.

levels.0: The page has no family drawing and no Hindi lines of introduction.
levels.1: A family drawing has a name or two beside the figures, but no sentence.
levels.2: A family drawing is joined by two or three Hindi lines introducing the family.
levels.3: Each family member's line tells one thing that person does, such as cooking or working.

rows.note: Named in the Hindi curriculum doc (month grid, one line per project); steps are suggested from that line, not copied. Children may draw an imagined or story family.

rows.name: Singing the train song with a beat (गीत पाठ, ताल के साथ गायन)
steps: Suggested: Write the train song on a chart.
Suggested: Sing it while clapping the beat and ask children to listen.
Suggested: Ask children to clap the beat while the educator sings.
Suggested: Sing and clap together as a class.
Suggested: Split into two groups and sing in turns.

levels.0: No clap lands on the beat and the song is not sung.
levels.1: Words are sung, but claps drift faster or slower than the beat of the train song.
levels.2: Claps fall on each beat all the way through the train song while the words are sung.
levels.3: Claps hold the beat when the song is sung faster or slower, or with a new pattern such as stamp-clap.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Reciting the poem 'कछुआ राजा' and a picture-based story
steps: Suggested: Read the poem 'कछुआ राजा' line by line with actions.
Suggested: Ask children to repeat each line with the actions.
Suggested: Cover lines one by one so children rely on memory.
Suggested: Ask pairs to recite the poem to each other.
Suggested: Show pictures from the poem and ask children to tell a story from them.

levels.0: No line of the poem is spoken once the chart is covered.
levels.1: The first two lines are recited, then the words stop or a line is skipped.
levels.2: All lines of 'कछुआ राजा' are recited in order from memory.
levels.3: The poem is recited with actions to the class, followed by a story told from its pictures.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Writing letters and making words with conjuncts (अक्षर लिखना व शब्द बनाना)
steps: Suggested: Show picture cards for words with a conjunct, such as स्कूल or चम्मच.
Suggested: Say each word aloud and break it into sounds.
Suggested: Show on the board how two letters join into one conjunct.
Suggested: Ask children to write the word for each picture in the notebook.
Suggested: Check each word against the picture together.

levels.0: No word is written beside any picture on the page.
levels.1: Letters of the word are written apart, with the conjunct halves not joined.
levels.2: The word for each picture is written with its conjunct joined correctly.
levels.3: A word with a conjunct not met in class is written correctly and used in a sentence.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Word-making activities with joined consonants (शब्द–निर्माण गतिविधियाँ)
steps: Suggested: Give each group a set of letter cards, including half-forms.
Suggested: Show a picture whose word has joined consonants, such as स्कूल.
Suggested: Ask groups to put the cards together to make the word.
Suggested: Ask them to read it aloud and write it in the notebook.
Suggested: Ask groups to make as many joined-consonant words as they can in five minutes.

levels.0: Letter cards lie loose on the desk and no two-consonant word is formed.
levels.1: Cards are put side by side to spell the word, but the half-form of the first consonant is missing.
levels.2: A word with two joined consonants is formed from letter cards and read aloud.
levels.3: Three different joined-consonant words are made in the time, one without a picture clue.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Making words that use र (र-युक्त शब्द बनाना)
steps: Suggested: Show the forms of र on the board, such as the mark above, the stroke below and the slanted stroke.
Suggested: Say words such as प्रेम, कर्म and ट्रक aloud.
Suggested: Give each pair letter cards including those forms of र.
Suggested: Ask pairs to build one word and read it aloud.
Suggested: Ask them to write the word in the notebook.

levels.0: No word with र is built and the र cards stay unused.
levels.1: A word is built with full र, but the changed form of र, such as the slanted stroke in प्र, is left out.
levels.2: A word with a form of र is made from letter cards and read aloud.
levels.3: Words with र above, below and as a slanted stroke are sorted into three groups after building them.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Making a story from a picture (चित्र देखकर कहानी बनाना)
steps: Suggested: Show a picture with many things going on.
Suggested: Ask what is there, who is there and where it is.
Suggested: Ask children to plan a beginning, middle and end.
Suggested: Ask each child to tell the story to a partner.
Suggested: Ask partners to swap and say one thing they liked.

levels.0: No spoken story follows the picture and the partner hears nothing.
levels.1: Things in the picture are listed one by one, with no event or order joining them.
levels.2: A made-up story linked to the picture is told to the partner, with a start and an end.
levels.3: A second story from a new picture adds what the characters say.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Making a story from pictures and words (चित्र और शब्द मिलाकर कहानी)
steps: Suggested: Lay out picture cards and a few given words.
Suggested: Ask children to put the pictures in an order that makes sense.
Suggested: Ask them to place the given words next to the pictures they fit.
Suggested: Ask them to tell the story to a partner.
Suggested: Ask them to write two or three lines of the story.

levels.0: No story is made from the picture and word cards.
levels.1: Pictures and words are laid in a row but with no story order.
levels.2: A short story is made that uses each given picture and word card in order.
levels.3: A second story is made from a new set of pictures and words.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; levels follow the reviewer's correction.

rows.name: Making sentences from many words (अनेक शब्दों से वाक्य बनाना)
steps: Suggested: Show picture cards with many things, such as बच्चे, पक्षी and फूल.
Suggested: Say the single and many form of each word.
Suggested: Ask children to say a sentence for each card.
Suggested: Ask them to write one sentence in the notebook.
Suggested: Read the sentences aloud together.

levels.0: No sentence is made from the picture card with many things.
levels.1: A sentence uses the single word, such as 'एक फूल', for a card showing many flowers.
levels.2: A sentence uses a plural word that fits the many things on the picture card.
levels.3: Sentences use plural words for new classroom pictures, each with a verb ending that matches.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Changing a word and writing a sentence (शब्द बदलकर वाक्य लिखना)
steps: Suggested: Write a sentence on the board, such as 'लड़का जाता है।'
Suggested: Underline the word that shows boy or girl.
Suggested: Change it to 'लड़की जाती है।' and read both.
Suggested: Give each child sentence cards to change in the same way.
Suggested: Ask children to write the changed sentences in the notebook.

levels.0: The sentence is copied unchanged or left blank, with no gender word altered.
levels.1: The naming word is changed from लड़का to लड़की, but the verb ending stays the same.
levels.2: The sentence is rewritten with the word in its other gender form and a matching verb ending.
levels.3: A sentence made up by the learner is changed to the other gender form with the matching ending.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Choosing the right word for a picture (चित्र के अनुसार सही शब्द चुनना)
steps: Suggested: Show a picture with three words written below it.
Suggested: Read the three words aloud together.
Suggested: Ask each child to circle or point to the word that matches.
Suggested: Repeat with five pictures.
Suggested: Ask children to say why they chose each word.

levels.0: No word is circled or pointed to under any picture.
levels.1: A word is chosen for easy pictures, but look-alike words such as कल and कमल get mixed up.
levels.2: The word that matches each picture is picked from the choice of words.
levels.3: A word is chosen for a picture from a new set, with a reason such as its first letter.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; cell gave only the topic.

rows.name: Fabric feel-and-sort and Journey of Cotton
steps: Feel cotton, wool, silk and jute and sort them.
Hear the story 'The Journey of Cotton'.
Play a matching game of fabrics and their uses.

levels.0: No fabric name is said when a cloth sample is held up.
levels.1: Cotton is named correctly, while wool and silk samples get called 'cloth' or 'soft'.
levels.2: Cotton, wool and silk samples are each named when held up.
levels.3: Fabrics worn today, such as the school uniform or a sweater, are named along with where each is used.

source.tab: Grade 1 Stitching and Weaving Science Curriculum

rows.name: Explore and name tools; safety chart; bead threading
steps: Explore and name the needle, thread and loom.
Create a safety rules chart.
Thread beads for fine motor skills (blunt needles and large beads for beginners).

levels.0: No tool is named when a needle, scissors or a loom is shown.
levels.1: Scissors and thread are named, while the needle and loom get a gesture or 'that thing'.
levels.2: A needle, thread, scissors and a loom are each named when held up.
levels.3: A tool is chosen for a job such as joining two pieces, and its name and use are said.

rows.name: Running stitch on paper, cloth and a greeting card
steps: Stitch on paper with pre-punched holes.
Stitch a straight line on cloth.
Create a greeting card with a stitched border.
rows.materials: Paper with punched holes, cloth, thick thread, blunt needle

levels.0: No stitch is made and the thread hangs loose from the fabric.
levels.1: Stitches are made but the spacing is uneven, with part of the line left unsewn.
levels.2: A line of running stitch goes up and down along the fabric with even spacing and ends in a knot.
levels.3: Running stitch follows a drawn curve or shape such as a leaf outline.

rows.name: Weaving a paper mat
steps: Weave a mat with colourful paper strips, over and under.
Explore checkered and striped patterns.
Display the finished mats and point out which pattern each one shows.

levels.0: The paper mat has no strips woven through it.
levels.1: Strips are woven in, but the over-under order breaks partway across the mat.
levels.2: The over-under pattern holds across the whole paper mat.
levels.3: A two-colour pattern is planned first and then woven across the mat without a break.

rows.name: Cardboard loom square
steps: Set up a simple cardboard loom.
Weave a small square fabric piece.
Pair weaker students with buddies; extend with diagonal weaving.

levels.0: The loom stays bare with no yarn passed through the strings.
levels.1: Yarn goes over and under for a few rows, then two rows repeat on the same side.
levels.2: Yarn goes over and under each string, and each row alternates with the one before.
levels.3: A band of woven rows in two colours covers the loom with straight edges.

rows.name: Food collage and kitchen safety role play
steps: Create a food collage from magazines, grouping food by plant or animal source.
Discuss and role-play kitchen safety scenarios.
Visit a school garden or local farm to see food sources.

levels.0: No source such as plant, tree or animal is named for the food picture.
levels.1: Fruit is linked to a tree, but milk and rice are said to come from the shop.
levels.2: Each pictured food is linked to where it comes from, such as milk to a cow and rice to a field.
levels.3: A food from the tiffin box is traced to its source, and one kitchen safety rule is said.

rows.name: Balanced meal plate
steps: Create a balanced meal plate using cutouts.
Taste and classify foods into food groups.
Discuss traditional Indian meals and their components.

levels.0: The plate stays empty and no food card is chosen for the meal.
levels.1: Cards are chosen but all come from one group, such as only sweets or only fruit.
levels.2: A plate holds cards from several groups, such as a grain, a vegetable and a protein, each named.
levels.3: A balanced tiffin is planned for a new meal such as breakfast, with a reason for each food.

rows.name: Fruit and vegetable tasting and chart
steps: Hold fruit and vegetable tasting sessions.
Create a fruit and vegetable chart.
Visit a local market to observe and identify produce.

levels.0: No fruit or vegetable is named when held up or pointed to.
levels.1: Mango and banana are named, while brinjal, okra and similar vegetables are not.
levels.2: Common fruits and vegetables grown in India, such as mango, banana, potato and tomato, are named correctly.
levels.3: Fruits and vegetables are sorted into two groups on a chart, with a colour or taste said for each.

rows.note: Check allergies before tasting.

rows.name: Grain and pulse collage; khichdi or dal
steps: Create a grain and pulse collage.
Cook a simple dish such as khichdi or dal.
Discuss regional variations in staple foods.

levels.0: No picture is placed in either column of the grains and pulses chart.
levels.1: Rice and wheat go under grains, but dal pictures are scattered across both columns.
levels.2: Pictures are sorted on the chart with each grain and each pulse in the right column.
levels.3: Foods made from them, such as roti or dal, are placed under the grain or pulse they come from.

rows.name: Lassi or paneer and a protein food chart
steps: Make a simple dairy-based dish such as lassi or paneer.
Create a protein food chart.
Discuss vegetarian and non-vegetarian protein sources.

levels.0: No food on the meal picture is circled or named as giving protein.
levels.1: Milk and egg are named, but dal, paneer or beans are left unmarked.
levels.2: Protein-rich foods on each meal picture, such as dal, paneer, eggs and milk, are named.
levels.3: A protein food is suggested for a meal that has none, with a reason such as 'it helps us grow'.

rows.name: Cardboard loom setup and diagonal weaving
steps: Suggested: Show a cardboard loom with notches cut along the top and bottom.
Suggested: Show how to wind the warp yarn around each notch.
Suggested: Tape the ends of the yarn at the back.
Suggested: Ask children to wind their own loom, step by step.
Suggested: Show how to weave the yarn diagonally across the strings.

levels.0: No yarn is wound on the cardboard loom.
levels.1: Warp yarn is wound on some notches but skips one, leaving uneven strings.
levels.2: Warp yarn is wound on every notch of the loom in the order the educator shows.
levels.3: A second loom is set up from memory and one diagonal row is woven.

rows.name: Stitch a pouch
steps: Stitch two pieces of cloth into a pouch.
Decorate with buttons or fabric paint.
Suggested: Check that the seams hold by gently pulling the pouch open.
rows.materials: Cloth, thread, buttons, fabric paint, templates

levels.0: No stitches join the two pieces of fabric.
levels.1: Stitches are uneven and the sides of the pouch gape open.
levels.2: The pouch is joined with running stitch and holds a small object.
levels.3: A button or fabric paint decoration is added to the stitched pouch.

rows.name: Whip and cross stitch embroidery
steps: Practise whip and cross stitches on old cloth.
Embroider a name or a pattern.
Suggested: Show the finished piece to a partner and name the stitch used.

levels.0: No whip stitch or cross stitch is on the fabric.
levels.1: Stitches are sewn, but they stay as straight lines and no X or wrap over the edge forms.
levels.2: A row of whip stitches or X-shaped cross stitches decorates the fabric.
levels.3: A pattern or initial is sewn using both whip and cross stitches.

rows.name: Video tour of weaving and paper designs
steps: Watch a video tour of weaving in India (Banarasi, Khadi).
Colour and weave paper designs inspired by Indian patterns.
Talk about which pattern or colour each child liked and why.

levels.0: No textile name is said for any sample or picture.
levels.1: One familiar textile, such as Khadi, is named, while others get 'cloth with dots'.
levels.2: Bandhani, Khadi and Banarasi are named correctly when each sample is shown.
levels.3: A textile is named and told apart by its look, such as dots for Bandhani or gold thread for Banarasi.
