rows.name: Exhibition and 'What I made and what I learned'
steps: Hold a stitching and weaving exhibition.
Each child gives an oral presentation: 'What I made and what I learned.'
Peer feedback and celebration.

levels.0: No spoken account is given beside the stitched or woven work on display.
levels.1: The work is named, such as 'my pouch', but how it was made is not said.
levels.2: The steps of making the work are told in order, from the start to the finished piece, with tools named.
levels.3: A hard part is told with what was done to fix it, and a visitor's question is answered.

source.tab: Grade 1 Stitching and Weaving Science Curriculum

rows.name: Cook a dish by different methods and compare
steps: Demonstrate boiling, steaming and frying.
Cook a dish using different methods and compare.
Discuss traditional Indian cooking techniques.

levels.0: No change to the food is described after the demonstration.
levels.1: A change such as 'soft' is noticed for boiled potato, but the method's name is not linked to it.
levels.2: Boiling and frying are named, each with what it did to the food, such as soft or crisp.
levels.3: A dish from home is linked to the cooking method used for it, with the change in the food said.

rows.name: Make pickles or jam; preservation chart
steps: Make pickles or jam.
Create a chart of preservation methods.
Discuss traditional Indian preservation techniques.
rows.materials: Fruit, salt, sugar, jars, chart paper

levels.0: No way of keeping food from spoiling is named for the preserved-food pictures.
levels.1: A fridge is named, but pickles and dried foods are called only 'tasty'.
levels.2: Pickling, drying and chilling are each named for the matching food picture.
levels.3: A way to keep a food at home, such as drying mangoes in the sun, is told with the reason it lasts longer.

rows.note: Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!E38.

rows.name: Festive dishes and festival food calendar
steps: Cook simple festive dishes.
Create a festival food calendar.
Discuss the role of food in celebrations.

levels.0: No festival and food are linked in any spoken sentence.
levels.1: A festive food is named, such as ladoo, but its festival is not.
levels.2: One sentence says why a festive food is made at its festival, such as ladoo for Diwali sweets.
levels.3: Sentences compare a festive food with an everyday food, or tell how the family makes it.

rows.name: The getting-ready algorithm
steps: Choose something you do every day, such as washing hands or packing the bag.
Draw each step in its own box, in order (Worksheet 1).
The educator performs the algorithm exactly as drawn.
Notice the missing step and say where it goes.
Pin the step-strips along the corridor.

levels.0: Picture cards stay shuffled and no step is named aloud.
levels.1: Some cards are in order, such as wet the brush then paste, but two steps stay swapped.
levels.2: The task's picture cards are laid in order, with first, next and last said for each.
levels.3: Steps for a second task such as packing a bag are put in order and a missing step is spotted.

rows.name: Bee-Bot programming basics
steps: Suggested: Show the Bee-Bot buttons: forward, back, left, right, go and clear.
Suggested: Place the Bee-Bot on the start square of the grid mat.
Suggested: Name a target square.
Suggested: Ask children to press the commands for the route and then Go.
Suggested: Press clear before the next try.

levels.0: No arrow button is pressed on the Bee-Bot before Go.
levels.1: Commands are entered but the Bee-Bot ends on the wrong square.
levels.2: The Bee-Bot reaches the given square on the grid mat.
levels.3: A longer route with at least one turn is programmed and run correctly.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!D147; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and unit; levels follow the reviewer's correction. The old keyword-list step was replaced. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!E11.

rows.name: Error wall: the broken version and the fix
steps: Put the broken version of an algorithm on the wall.
Write the fix beside it with the child's name on both.
Talk about why mistakes are the learning.

levels.0: No command card is pointed to when the robot's path goes wrong.
levels.1: The wrong path is noticed, but the pointed card is a correct one next to the faulty one.
levels.2: The faulty command in the instruction cards is pointed to after the robot's wrong path.
levels.3: The faulty card is swapped for the right one and the robot then reaches the goal square.

rows.name: Collecting data: surveys and recording
steps: Suggested: Pick a survey question such as favourite fruit.
Suggested: Draw a chart with a column for each choice.
Suggested: Ask each child to answer and make a tally mark under the choice.
Suggested: Group the marks in fives.
Suggested: Count the totals and say which choice has the most.

levels.0: The chart has no mark for any answer.
levels.1: Marks are made for answers, but they are single marks with no groups of five and one is missed in the count.
levels.2: Each answer is recorded as a tally mark on the chart under the right choice.
levels.3: Tally marks are grouped in fives, totalled, and a most-chosen answer is stated.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and unit; syllabus line gave only Focus and Key Concepts.

rows.name: Design a robot for a job in school
steps: Find where robots actually work.
Design a robot for a real job in this school (Worksheet 4).
Build it from boxes.
Label what it senses and what it does, plus three instructions it follows.

levels.0: Machine pictures get no job words and the robot picture gets no sensor name.
levels.1: Machine jobs are named only after the educator points to the moving part, and no sensor is named.
levels.2: A job done by a machine alone, such as sweeping a floor, is named from a picture, along with a robot sensor.
levels.3: A machine job and its sensor are named for a picture not used in the lesson, such as a door that opens.

rows.name: Art is all around us: school walk and class mural
steps: Circle time: 'What is Art?'.
Show real objects or photos (buildings, fabrics, packaging).
Walk round the school and sketch patterns, textures and colours on clipboards.
Compile the sketches into a large Class Mural.
rows.materials: Clipboards, sketch paper, crayons, markers, scissors, glue, A3 paper

levels.0: The page stays blank, or holds scribbles that do not match the object on the table.
levels.1: A sketch shows only one part of the object, such as the handle, and the overall outline is missing.
levels.2: An outline sketch of the object on the table shows its main shape and at least one detail.
levels.3: A second object from home is sketched with its own shape and details, drawn from looking at it.

source.cell: Week 1: Introduction to Visual Arts & Exploration

rows.name: Let's follow the line: Line Monster
steps: Warm-up: draw how you feel using only lines.
Show line art by Kandinsky and Paul Klee.
Practise straight, zigzag, wavy, spiral and dashed lines on large paper.
Make a Line Monster or Line Jungle using all types.

levels.0: Only one kind of line fills the page and no feeling is linked to any line.
levels.1: Two line kinds appear, but they are not matched to feelings or the match is said only after a hint.
levels.2: Three line kinds, such as wavy for calm and zigzag for angry, are each linked to a feeling.
levels.3: Lines drawn for a new feeling, such as surprise, are explained by their shape.

rows.name: Shapes everywhere: shape hunt and shape scene
steps: Circle time: find shapes in pictures of nature, buildings and animals.
Do a shape hunt with a checklist.
Draw a scene using only shapes.
Optional shape collage.
rows.materials: Shape stencils, glue, coloured paper, scissors, markers

levels.0: The page has no shapes taken from nature, only loose marks.
levels.1: One nature shape, such as a leaf, appears, but the rest of the page has no linked shapes.
levels.2: Leaf, shell or flower shapes are drawn and arranged into one picture.
levels.3: Shapes from a different nature object, such as a feather, are used in a fresh picture and described.

source.cell: Week 3: Shapes in Nature and Art

rows.name: Let's mix it up: primary colours
steps: Read a picture book such as Mouse Paint.
Mix two primary colours to find secondaries.
Make a Magic Colour Wheel.
Create a group mural with primary and secondary colours.
rows.materials: Tempera paints, palettes, brushes, aprons, colour wheel charts

levels.0: Paint stays unmixed on the palette and no new colour is on the page.
levels.1: A muddy brown appears because all three paints were mixed, or the mixed colour goes unnamed.
levels.2: Orange, green or purple patches appear, each made from exactly two primary paints.
levels.3: A named secondary colour is made again from two primaries on request, with the pair said aloud.

rows.name: New colours, new worlds: secondary colours
steps: Recap the primary colours.
Give only red, yellow and blue and ask children to invent green, orange and purple.
Paint a landscape or fantasy creature using only secondary colours.
Dry the paintings and discuss the feelings the colours give.
rows.materials: Tempera paints, palettes, A3 sheets, aprons, water jars

levels.0: Only primary colours appear and no mixing is on the palette.
levels.1: One secondary colour is mixed with a hand from the educator on the palette, and the rest is left unmixed.
levels.2: Orange, green and purple mixed by the painter all appear in one painted picture.
levels.3: Brown or a lighter shade is made by mixing a secondary with another colour, and the mix is told.

source.cell: Week 5: Secondary Colours and Colour Play

rows.name: Hot or Not? Warm World and Cool World
steps: Show warm and cool artworks.
Group objects by temperature (sun vs water, fire vs ice).
Paint a Warm World and a Cool World.
Discuss how each feels.

levels.0: Colours on the page are mixed with no sign of a warm or cool group.
levels.1: Warm colours are painted but a cool colour sits in the same scene, so the mood is unclear.
levels.2: A hot-day picture uses reds, oranges and yellows only, or a cold-day picture uses blues and greens only.
levels.3: A scene for a new mood, such as a sleepy night, is painted with a chosen colour group and told.

rows.name: How does it feel? Texture rubbings and Texture Monster
steps: Feel fabric, leaves, sandpaper and cotton and say describing words.
Make texture rubbings with crayons.
Make a Texture Monster from collaged material and rubbings.
Share monster names and their texture powers.
rows.materials: Fabric scraps, bark, foil, crayons, glue, scissors

levels.0: No texture marks are drawn, only a plain outline or a blank page.
levels.1: One texture is drawn, but every area uses the same marks, so rough and smooth look alike.
levels.2: Two textures, one felt and one seen, are drawn with different marks and each is named.
levels.3: A rubbing is matched to its drawn texture, or a new texture is drawn with fitting marks.

rows.name: Nature's patterns: leaf rubbings
steps: Examine leaves closely: veins, edges, symmetry.
Make leaf rubbings with crayons or oil pastels.
Use the rubbings to make an animal collage.
Optional: print leaves with paint.
rows.materials: Leaves, crayons, pastels, paints, large paper

levels.0: The artwork has no leaf shapes, and neither vein lines nor texture marks.
levels.1: A leaf outline appears, but veins or texture are missing from it.
levels.2: A real leaf is shown by its outline, vein lines and a rubbed texture.
levels.3: A second leaf of a different kind is shown with its own vein pattern and texture, and the difference is said.

source.cell: Week 8: Lines and Textures in Nature — Leaf Art

rows.name: Make it repeat: pattern borders and prints
steps: Show patterns in textiles and tiles.
Practise red-blue-red-blue and circle-square-triangle patterns.
Make a pattern border for a card or a name.
Optional: print patterns with bottle caps, stamps or blocks.
rows.materials: Stamps, sponge blocks, paints, paper strips, markers

levels.0: Marks on the strip are scattered with no repeat at all.
levels.1: The pattern repeats twice and then breaks, or one colour is skipped.
levels.2: A shape or colour repeats in the same order across the whole row.
levels.3: A pattern with a two-part unit, such as circle then triangle, runs the full strip.

rows.name: Pencil shading: hatching, cross-hatching, stippling
steps: Demo shading with a light-to-dark gradient strip.
Explore pencil pressure and make a gradient.
Teach hatching, cross-hatching and stippling.
Pick 1–2 real textures (bark, cloth, brick) and draw them in pencil.
Texture hunt: find 3 textures in the classroom.

levels.0: The shape is left unshaded, or the pencil marks cover it as a flat grey smear.
levels.1: One shading technique is tried, but the marks are uneven or cross the outline.
levels.2: Hatching, cross-hatching or stippling is visible inside the shape, in the right marks.
levels.3: Two techniques are used in two areas of one drawing to show light and dark.

source.cell: Week 10: Drawing Techniques — Shading and Texture

rows.name: Looking closely: still life drawing
steps: Show simple still-life artworks.
Set up a mini still life of 3–4 objects per table.
Sketch and colour the setup focusing on shape, size and position.
Display the drawings beside a photo of the objects.
rows.materials: Real objects (fruit, toys, vases), sketchbooks, pencils, pastels, magnifying glasses

levels.0: No objects from the table are on the page.
levels.1: One object is drawn, but the second is left out or sits in the wrong place.
levels.2: All table objects appear in their positions, with their main shapes recognisable.
levels.3: The group is drawn again from a different seat so the overlaps change.

source.cell: Week 11: Drawing from Observation — Still Life

rows.name: Funny faces with shapes
steps: Show Picasso's cubist portraits.
Name the parts of the face and experiment with size, shape and colour.
Draw or collage a face using only shapes.
Name and describe the abstract person.
rows.materials: Coloured paper, scissors, glue, mirrors, crayons

levels.0: No face is assembled, only a pile of loose shapes.
levels.1: A face made of shapes is present, but the feeling it shows is not clear.
levels.2: A shape-built face shows a clear feeling through its mouth or eyes.
levels.3: A second face with a new feeling is made by changing one shape, and the change is told.

source.cell: Week 12: Shape and Story — Abstract Faces

rows.name: Dream house with a pop-up
steps: Circle time: 'If you could build your dream house, what would it have?'.
Show photos of unique houses (igloo, treehouse, houseboat).
Draw a basic house with 2D shapes, then make a pop-up.
Share and explain the house to the class.
rows.materials: A4 sheets, pencils, markers, scissors, glue, rulers, scrap paper

levels.0: The house is drawn as a single flat shape with no side wall.
levels.1: A front wall is drawn, but the side wall or roof is joined in a way that looks flat.
levels.2: A house appears with a front wall, a side wall and a roof joined to show depth.
levels.3: Windows or a door are added on the side wall and shown at an angle.

rows.name: Draw what you love: favourite animal in its habitat
steps: Talk about favourite animals and where they live.
Share books or images of animals.
Draw the favourite animal in its habitat.
Write a line about what the animal loves doing.
rows.materials: Drawing paper, colored pencils, crayons, reference images

levels.0: Boxes are empty or have no animal drawn.
levels.1: The animal appears in each box, but nothing changes from box to box.
levels.2: Three boxes show the same animal doing different things that make a story in order.
levels.3: A problem and an ending are added across the boxes and told aloud.

source.cell: Week 14: Storytelling with Art — My Favorite Animal

rows.name: Clay creatures
steps: Show real clay sculptures or toys.
Discuss what makes a creature: eyes, legs, wings, tails.
Demonstrate rolling, pinching and coiling.
Make a Clay Creature and label it with a name and description.
rows.materials: Air-dry clay, damp cloths, clay boards, water bowls

levels.0: No clay form is made, only a flat or unshaped lump.
levels.1: A lump with no animal features, such as a head or legs, sits on the board.
levels.2: A clay animal shows a head, a body and legs joined together.
levels.3: Fur or scales are added with a tool and the marks are told.

rows.name: Dream collage
steps: Read a short dream-themed picture book or poem.
Ask 'What do you dream about? What's your happy place?'.
Draw the basic layout of the dream.
Layer fabric, paper and lace onto the picture.
Label with a dream title and a short sentence.
rows.materials: Glue, scissors, coloured paper, magazine cuttings, yarn, lace, net

levels.0: Only the base paper is on the page and no layers are stuck on.
levels.1: One material is stuck down, but a second layer is missing.
levels.2: Three layers of different materials are stuck on to show a dream scene.
levels.3: A dream's feeling is told and one chosen material is explained as fitting it.

rows.name: Paper weaving mat
steps: Show woven mats and baskets.
Demonstrate vertical slits and horizontal strips.
Choose two colours and weave a piece.
Trim and mount for display.
rows.materials: Pre-cut base sheets, colour strips, glue, tape, scissors

levels.0: No strips are woven and the base remains uncovered.
levels.1: A strip is woven over and under for one row, and the next row repeats the same moves.
levels.2: Strips go over and under in alternating rows across the whole base to form a pattern.
levels.3: Two colours of strips are woven so a checker pattern is visible.

rows.name: Warli story scenes
steps: Show simplified Warli samples.
Discuss story scenes: festivals, nature, homes, animals.
Draw with white paint on brown chart.
Add Warli stick figures and patterns.
rows.materials: Brown paper, white paint or gel pens, fine brushes

levels.0: White circle heads and triangle bodies are absent from the dark paper.
levels.1: Figures appear, but they are drawn as ordinary people instead of circle and triangle shapes.
levels.2: A story scene is drawn with triangle bodies, circle heads and lines.
levels.3: A new scene, such as harvest, is drawn with extra figures and described.

source.cell: Week 18: Folk Art – Warli Story Scenes

rows.name: Stamp a garden with potato and okra
steps: Show print examples.
Demonstrate potato and vegetable stamping to make leaves and flowers.
Make a stamped garden.
Add details with pen or brush once dry.
rows.materials: Potatoes, okra, sponge bits, paints, brushes, A3 paper

levels.0: Stamp prints are missing, so the page shows only blank paper or paint dabs.
levels.1: Prints appear, but they are smudged or one stamp is repeated over the page.
levels.2: Several stamps form a garden picture with flowers, grass and leaves.
levels.3: Overlapping prints or a new stamp are used to add depth, and the choice is told.

source.cell: Week 19: Printing Techniques – Stamp a Garden

rows.name: Nature rubbing collage
steps: Take a nature walk to collect bark, leaves and stones.
Demonstrate rubbings with crayons.
Do rubbings and cut and arrange them into an artwork.
Mount as a 'Nature Texture Story'.
rows.materials: White paper, crayons, nature objects, glue, scissors

levels.0: Crayon rubbings of leaves or bark are missing from the sheet to cut up.
levels.1: Rubbings are made, but they are not cut or layered onto a base.
levels.2: A collage of layered rubbings shows two or more nature textures.
levels.3: Rubbings are arranged to form a picture such as a tree, with the texture named for each part.

source.cell: Week 20: Textural Art – Nature Rubbing Collage

rows.name: Butterfly prints
steps: Show butterfly images and discuss wing symmetry.
Fold paper in half, open it, paint shapes on one side, fold again and press.
Compare 'matching halves' with a peer.
Play Mirror Me: copy the educator's symmetrical poses.
rows.materials: Folded A4 sheets, poster paints, brushes, aprons

levels.0: The paper is not folded and no print appears.
levels.1: A print shows on one side, but the second side has smudges or a gap.
levels.2: A folded print shows two wings that match each other across the fold.
levels.3: Another picture, such as a leaf, is printed in halves and the fold line is shown.

rows.name: Animal expressions: shapes and lines
steps: Discuss animal features: ears, fur, feathers, tails.
Pick a favourite animal.
Sketch and colour it with a background.

levels.0: An animal body made of shapes and lines is absent from the paper.
levels.1: An animal is drawn, but either shapes or lines are missing.
levels.2: Shapes make the animal's body and lines add legs, tail or whiskers.
levels.3: A second animal is drawn using a new set of shapes and described.

rows.name: Paper creatures
steps: Practise tearing paper slowly.
Fold a basic fan or shape.
Make a paper creature using tearing, folding and cutting.
Draw eyes and decorate it.
Game: 'Tear Me a Rainbow'.
rows.materials: Coloured paper, safety scissors, glue, marker pens

levels.0: Paper stays flat and uncut, with no folded, torn or cut shape made.
levels.1: A torn or cut shape is begun, but its edges are left unfinished.
levels.2: A finished paper shape is made by folding, tearing or cutting.
levels.3: Two methods are combined in a single paper shape.

source.cell: Week 23: Paper Play – Folding, Tearing, Cutting

rows.name: Matisse cut-out collage
steps: Show Matisse cut-outs: 'painting with scissors'.
Make an abstract collage from coloured paper.
Add a title to the work.

levels.0: No cut shapes are stuck on the page.
levels.1: Cut shapes are stuck down but follow outlines of real things only, with no free-form shapes.
levels.2: Free-form cutouts in bright colours are glued down to form an abstract collage.
levels.3: Cutout shapes are overlapped, and the collage is linked to Matisse's style.

source.cell: Week 24: Inspired by Artists – Henri Matisse

rows.name: Who works where? role play and floor plan
steps: Role play 'Who works where?' (kitchen, library, principal's office).
Draw a floor plan of the classroom or a house.
Fill in a home-school comparison chart.

levels.0: Neither a room of the house picture nor a school area gets a name.
levels.1: Kitchen is named, yet bedroom and bathroom stay unnamed until the educator points.
levels.2: Kitchen, bedroom and bathroom are each named on the house picture, with a school area added.
levels.3: A room at the child's own home is named and its use is compared with a school area.

source.cell: Fortnight 1 & 2: My Home and My School

rows.name: Neighbourhood tour, helper puppets and market story
steps: Take a field trip or watch a video tour of the post office, fire station and similar places.
Make community helper puppets.
Sequence the story 'A trip to the market'.
rows.materials: Puppet-making materials, video or field trip

levels.0: Place pictures get no name and no use is said.
levels.1: A shop is named from its picture, but what people do there is left unsaid.
levels.2: Park, clinic or shop is named from a picture and its use is told, such as buying food.
levels.3: A place near the child's home is named with its use, and a second place is compared.

rows.name: Classroom treasure hunt and floor arrow path
steps: Run a classroom treasure hunt using directional words.
Create a path using arrows on the floor.
Sort landmarks into natural and man-made.
Use compass cards and blocks.

levels.0: When asked where the toy is, no position word is said.
levels.1: Near and far are said for the toy, but left and right are swapped.
levels.2: A toy's place is said with a position word such as left of the door or near the board.
levels.3: Directions with left and right guide a partner to a hidden object in a new spot.

rows.name: Classroom map with symbols and My tiny town
steps: Create a map of the classroom with symbols.
Match objects (tree, desk) to map icons.
Craft 'My tiny town' map.

levels.0: Symbols on the map are passed over without any reading.
levels.1: A symbol is named from its shape alone, and the key is left unused.
levels.2: A symbol such as a door is read by finding it in the key beside the map.
levels.3: A symbol on a new map is read from its own key, and a new symbol is drawn for a place.

rows.name: Flag colouring, state flashcards and India map puzzle
steps: Colour the flag and take a quiz.
Play state flashcard games.
Assemble a jigsaw-style map puzzle of India.

levels.0: India is not picked out on the world map.
levels.1: India is found on the world map only after its outline is traced by the educator.
levels.2: India is pointed to on a world map, with a city or state found on the India map.
levels.3: A different country is compared with India on the same map, using the words big or small.

rows.name: Family drawing, family tree and role play
steps: Draw a family (own, imagined or from a story).
Circle time: 'Who is in your family?' — each child shares only what they wish.
Build a simple family tree of two or three levels.
Role play mother, father, sibling.
Talk about grandparents as 'before time'.

levels.0: No family member from the photo is named.
levels.1: One older family member from the past is named.
levels.2: Grandparents and one earlier generation are named from the family photo.
levels.3: One thing about life when grandparents were young is told.

rows.note: Family sharing is optional; nobody is asked for home details.

rows.name: Slate writing and old-school role play
steps: Try writing on a slate.
Role play an old school and a school now.
Draw the classroom.

levels.0: No difference between now and long ago is said or drawn.
levels.1: One difference is said after the educator points to it, and the other picture is left uncompared.
levels.2: Two pictures are compared and one difference is named for each, such as a slate and a tablet.
levels.3: A new pair of pictures is compared, with the changes said and a reason given.

rows.name: Match symbols to meanings; design your own symbol
steps: Match symbol cards to meaning cards.
Hunt for the symbols in the textbook.
Design your own symbol.

levels.0: None of the national symbol pictures is named.
levels.1: A symbol such as the peacock is named, but its kind (bird, flower) is wrong.
levels.2: A national symbol is named from a picture, such as the tiger as the national animal.
levels.3: A reason a symbol matters to India is told in a sentence of the child's own.

rows.name: Festival calendar, dress-up relay and no-fire Diwali sweets
steps: Make a festival calendar.
Run a traditional dress-up relay.
Make Diwali sweets without fire.
rows.materials: Calendar chart, dress-up clothes, sweet ingredients

levels.0: No festival custom is told for the pictures.
levels.1: A festival is named but nothing about how it is celebrated is said.
levels.2: A festival custom is told from a picture, such as lighting lamps at Diwali.
levels.3: A festival is compared with another, with one custom and one difference told.

rows.name: Season wheel, puppet dress-up and rain in a jar
steps: Make a season wheel.
Dress a puppet for summer, monsoon and winter.
Make rain in a jar.
rows.materials: Paper plate, puppet, jar, water, shaving foam

levels.0: Summer, monsoon and winter pictures are shown but no season name is said.
levels.1: One season is named but the others are mixed up.
levels.2: Summer, monsoon and winter are named from a picture of each.
levels.3: A season's features are told, such as rain in the monsoon, with clothes to match.

rows.name: Sand tray landforms and foil river
steps: Model the Himalayas and the Thar desert in a sand tray.
Simulate a river flowing with foil.
Match pictures of landforms.

levels.0: Mountain, river, plain and desert pictures are shown with no landform word said.
levels.1: A mountain is named, but a river is called by the wrong name.
levels.2: A mountain, river, plain or desert is named from a picture.
levels.3: A landform is placed on a map of India and its features are told.

rows.name: Animal miming and habitat box
steps: Play a sound-and-movement miming game for domestic, wild and farm animals.
Build a habitat box.
Visit a garden or take a virtual nature walk.

levels.0: Animal cards are left without sorting into groups.
levels.1: Domestic animals are sorted correctly, but wild and farm animals are mixed.
levels.2: Cards are placed into domestic, wild and farm hoops, such as a cow in farm.
levels.3: A new animal card is placed in a hoop and a reason for the choice is told.

source.cell: Fortnight 19 & 20: Plants and Animals Around Us

rows.name: Yoga introduction and Suryanamaskar
steps: Suggested: Lay mats in a line and begin with three slow breaths.
Suggested: Show the 12 positions of Suryanamaskar one at a time and say each name.
Suggested: Ask children to copy each position and hold it for three breaths.
Suggested: Walk round and remind children to keep a straight back and relaxed shoulders.
Suggested: End with rest lying on the mat.

levels.0: Poses collapse at once, with the back rounded and no hold of even one breath.
levels.1: A pose is held for a count of three, but the back stays bent or shoulders lifted until the educator corrects it.
levels.2: Each pose in the Suryanamaskar round is held with a straight back and still feet for three slow breaths.
levels.3: Held poses keep the straight back while a neighbour's posture is described aloud and a correction is suggested.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Eye-hand, hand-leg coordination and eye exercises
steps: Suggested: Start with eye exercises: look up, down, left and right slowly with the head still.
Suggested: Ask each child to bounce and catch a soft ball with both hands.
Suggested: Have children throw a beanbag at a mark on the wall.
Suggested: Do a hand-leg move: march and touch each raised knee with the opposite hand.
Suggested: Finish by resting the eyes by covering them with warm palms.

levels.0: Ball or beanbag drops to the floor on every attempt, and the exercise is not copied.
levels.1: Catches happen only after the educator throws from close by and counts aloud.
levels.2: An eye-hand exercise such as bounce and catch is repeated as shown, with the ball caught three times in a row.
levels.3: Hand-leg moves like touching a raised knee with the opposite hand are added to the catch, keeping the rhythm for ten counts.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Designing a playground game of the month
steps: Suggested: Put children into groups of four and ask each group to pick a game for the month.
Suggested: Walk the playground and mark the ground with chalk, measuring by paces.
Suggested: Ask groups to decide the total players and the player kit.
Suggested: Help each group say or draw two or three rules and make a point table.
Suggested: Play the game once and let groups change a rule if needed.

levels.0: No game idea is named and no rule is spoken to the group.
levels.1: A game idea is named and one rule is said, but the number of players or the way to score is missing.
levels.2: An invented game is explained with its rules, player number and a filled-in point table.
levels.3: A rule is changed after a trial play with the reason stated, and the changed game is taught to another group.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Eurythmy and Independence Day performance and dance
steps: Suggested: Play music with a clear beat and have children clap the beat.
Suggested: Teach the eurythmy movements to the rhythm, stepping and arms.
Suggested: Teach the Independence Day dance in short parts.
Suggested: Practise in lines first and then all together.
Suggested: Finish with a run-through with the music.

levels.0: Hands and feet stay out of time with the music, with no clap or step on the beat.
levels.1: Clapping lands on the beat, but steps drift off it until a partner counts aloud.
levels.2: Steps and arm movements in the dance land on the beat of the music through the whole practice.
levels.3: A new tune at a different speed is danced with steps still on the beat, and the pattern is shown to a partner.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Eurythmy and meditation
steps: Suggested: Sit in a circle and take three slow breaths.
Suggested: Do the eurythmy movements to a slow beat.
Suggested: Clap and step the rhythm together.
Suggested: Return to sitting and count breaths up to ten for the meditation.
Suggested: Share one word for how the body feels.
rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm. Character/wellbeing activity (meditation): no graded levels; look-fors only.
look_fors: moves in time with the beat of the music
stays still and quiet during the meditation without being reminded
joins in the breathing counted by the educator

rows.name: Balance practice
steps: Suggested: Mark lines on the floor.
Suggested: Show a one-leg stand and ask children to copy it.
Suggested: Ask children to stand on one leg while the class counts to five aloud.
Suggested: Walk along the line heel to toe.
Suggested: Try the stand with arms out and then with arms folded while partners count.

levels.0: Lifted foot drops down again before the count of two.
levels.1: One-leg stand lasts to a count of three, with arms waving or a hand on a friend.
levels.2: A balance is held steadily on one leg for a count of five without the lifted foot touching down.
levels.3: The balance is held for a count of ten with arms folded or eyes on a spot, and a harder version is made up.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Skipping with a rope and dancing to different rhythms
steps: Suggested: Set out one rope per child with plenty of space between children.
Suggested: Show how to hold the handles and turn the rope over the head.
Suggested: Let children practise jumping with two feet and then with alternate feet.
Suggested: Count jumps in a row aloud.
Suggested: Play fast and slow music and dance to each beat.

levels.0: Rope stays by the feet or tangles, with no jump made as the rope passes.
levels.1: Rope is turned and one or two jumps land over it, but the rope stops after each jump.
levels.2: Rope passes under the feet in a run of five or more jumps in a row.
levels.3: Jumping continues through a slow then a fast beat, with the speed changing with the music, for ten jumps.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Paper cutting on fine lines and folding paper
steps: Suggested: Give each child a pair of scissors and a paper with thick lines drawn on it.
Suggested: Show how to hold the paper with one hand and cut slowly.
Suggested: Cut along the straight lines first and then the curved lines.
Suggested: Show how to fold paper in half and corner to corner, matching the edges.
Suggested: Press the fold flat with a thumb.

levels.0: Cut edge wanders far from the drawn line, and folds do not meet at the edges.
levels.1: Cutting stays on the line for the straight part but strays on the curve.
levels.2: Cut edge follows the drawn line, and folded corners meet the edge with a flat crease.
levels.3: A new shape such as a zigzag or a boat fold is cut or folded from a picture instruction with a clean edge.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Morning eurythmy and meditation
steps: Suggested: Gather in a morning circle on mats.
Suggested: Settle with three quiet breaths.
Suggested: Teach the eurythmy movement sequence and repeat it.
Suggested: Practise with music.
Suggested: Close with meditation: sit still with eyes closed and count five breaths.
rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm. Character/wellbeing activity (meditation): no graded levels; look-fors only.
look_fors: moves in time with the beat of the music
stays still and quiet during the meditation without being reminded
joins in the breathing counted by the educator

rows.name: Balance and rotation skills; rope skipping
steps: Suggested: Set up three stations: a balance line, a rotation spot and a rope area.
Suggested: Divide the class into groups and rotate them through the stations.
Suggested: At the balance station, stand on one leg and count.
Suggested: At the rotation station, turn a full circle on the spot and land steady.
Suggested: At the rope station, practise skipping.

levels.0: Standing leg wobbles and the lifted foot lands before a count of two at the balance station.
levels.1: A balance on one leg is held for three counts only when a hand touches the wall.
levels.2: At the balance station one leg stands steady for a count of five after a full turn on the spot.
levels.3: Balance is held after a rotation with the arms folded and the count reaching ten, followed by a rope jump.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm. Rubric follows the first linked objective (balance).

rows.name: Making outdoor activity cards
steps: Suggested: Give each group blank cards, pencils and crayons.
Suggested: Ask the group to think of an outdoor game or exercise.
Suggested: Draw a picture on the front and write the name at the top.
Suggested: Say or write one to three rules on the back.
Suggested: Swap cards with another group and play one.

levels.0: Blank card has no picture, name or rule on it.
levels.1: Card shows a picture and name, but the rules are told by an adult or left out.
levels.2: Outdoor activity card has the game's name, a picture and its rules spoken aloud to the group.
levels.3: A card swapped with another group is played as written, and one of its rules is improved and written again.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Dodging, walking in different directions and an obstacle course
steps: Suggested: Set out cones, hoops and a low bench as an obstacle course.
Suggested: Walk through the course slowly forwards, sideways and backwards.
Suggested: Play a dodge game by dodging a partner's tag.
Suggested: Run the course one child at a time.
Suggested: Call change direction at points along the course.

levels.0: Cones are knocked over or skipped, and no turn is made when the direction is called.
levels.1: Course is completed, but direction changes happen only when a helper stands and points.
levels.2: Obstacle course is crossed with a turn left, right or backwards on each call and no cone knocked.
levels.3: A course built by the group is run in a new order, calling out each direction change before making it.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Cat and Mouse (a chasing game from China)
steps: Suggested: Choose a cat and a mouse; the others form a circle holding hands.
Suggested: Explain that the cat chases the mouse in and out of the ring.
Suggested: Let the circle lift arms to let the mouse in.
Suggested: Swap roles when the mouse is caught.
Suggested: Ask what happens when the mouse is caught to check the rules.

levels.0: Chase starts before the signal or stops as roles are ignored.
levels.1: Chasing follows the rules for the first round, then tagging happens outside the ring.
levels.2: Cat and mouse stay within the game's rules, with roles swapped on a catch.
levels.3: Rules of Cat and Mouse are explained to a newcomer, and a changed rule is tried out.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Formal introduction to yoga: breath, animal yoga, adventure story, savasana
steps: Suggested: Lie on mats with a hand on the belly and feel the breath.
Suggested: Do animal poses such as cat-cow and downward dog.
Suggested: Tell a short adventure story and move through poses as the story goes.
Suggested: End lying still in savasana for one minute.

levels.0: Poses end after one breath with children rolling or sitting up off the mat.
levels.1: Cat-cow and downward dog are held for two breaths, but the back droops until corrected.
levels.2: Each animal pose is held with a long spine and relaxed neck for three breaths.
levels.3: Savasana is held still, and a pose from the adventure story is named and held without being shown.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: B.K.S. Iyengar fundamentals: Tadasana, Mountain pose, Warrior 1 and 2
steps: Suggested: Stand tall in Tadasana with feet together and lift the toes.
Suggested: Break down Mountain pose: feet, knees, tummy, shoulders, arms.
Suggested: Step the feet wide and turn one foot out for Warrior 1 and Warrior 2.
Suggested: Ask a partner to check alignment from the side.
Suggested: Hold each pose for three breaths.

levels.0: Tadasana ends within one breath, with feet apart and shoulders hunched.
levels.1: Warrior 1 and 2 are held with the front knee over the ankle only after the educator adjusts the stance.
levels.2: Tadasana, Mountain and Warrior poses are held for three breaths with ankles, hips and shoulders in one line.
levels.3: A partner's alignment in Warrior 2 is checked from the side and one correction is spoken aloud.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Preparation for Sports Day
steps: Suggested: Divide the class into teams with colours.
Suggested: Practise one race, such as a relay, with start and finish lines.
Suggested: Teach the rules: wait for go, stay in lane, pass the baton.
Suggested: Practise a team cheer.
Suggested: Run a mock event.

levels.0: Teams break the start line before the signal, and the rules of the race are not followed.
levels.1: Race rules are followed in the first heat, then lanes or baton passes are lost in the next.
levels.2: A team relay is run following its rules: start on the signal, stay in lane and pass the baton.
levels.3: Rules of a Sports Day event are explained to another team, and a rule broken is spotted and named.

rows.note: Named in Monthly Detailed Plan!F28; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!G22.

rows.name: Catch the Dragon's Tail
steps: Suggested: Line the children up holding the shoulders in front; the last one tucks a bib into the waist as the tail.
Suggested: Ask the front child (the head) to try to tag the tail.
Suggested: Keep the line joined at all times.
Suggested: Move a tagged tail to the head of the line.
Suggested: Play again with a new head.

levels.0: Line breaks apart at once, and the tail is never chased.
levels.1: Line holds together for a few steps, and the head chases the tail only after reminders.
levels.2: Dragon line stays joined while the head chases the tail, and a tagged tail moves to the head.
levels.3: Rules of Catch the Dragon's Tail are taught to a new group, and a safe-play rule is added.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: What's the time, Mr Wolf?
steps: Suggested: Choose a wolf to stand at one end; the others line up at the far end.
Suggested: Have children chant What's the time, Mr Wolf?
Suggested: Let the wolf call a time such as three o'clock and children take that many steps.
Suggested: When the wolf calls dinnertime, the wolf chases the others back.
Suggested: Make a tagged child the next wolf.

levels.0: Steps are taken with no count, and the chant is not said.
levels.1: Chant is said, but the number of steps differs from the time called.
levels.2: Mr Wolf's called time matches the number of steps taken, and everyone runs back at dinnertime.
levels.3: A new wolf calls an unusual time, the group counts the steps aloud, and the rules are recalled.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Duck, duck, goose
steps: Suggested: Sit in a circle facing in.
Suggested: Ask one child to walk round tapping heads and saying duck.
Suggested: Have the walker say goose on one head; the goose chases the walker.
Suggested: Let the walker try to reach the empty gap before being tagged.
Suggested: Make the goose the next walker.

levels.0: Children stay seated without any tap or chase, or run before goose is called.
levels.1: Tapping and saying duck is done, but the goose rule for chasing needs a reminder.
levels.2: Duck is said on each tap, goose starts the chase, and the walker sits in the empty gap.
levels.3: Rules of duck, duck, goose are explained to a new player, with a change such as hopping tried.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Name Chase
steps: Suggested: Stand in a circle.
Suggested: Have the chaser call a name and run round the circle.
Suggested: Let the named child chase and try to tag the first child before returning to the gap.
Suggested: Remind children to call classmates by name kindly.
Suggested: Swap roles and play again.

levels.0: Names are not called aloud and no chase begins.
levels.1: A name is called, but the chase starts before the named child is ready, or runs the wrong way.
levels.2: Called name starts the chase, the named runner leaves the spot, and the game continues in turn.
levels.3: Many names are called in order across the circle with the rule of waiting kept, and a new rule is added.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the educators' cell; detail invented, educator should confirm.

rows.name: Word of the Day
steps: Suggested: Write the word of the day on the board and read it together.
Suggested: Show what it means with a picture or action.
Suggested: Ask children to say it in a sentence with a partner.
Suggested: Write the word on a sticky note and use it again by the end of the day.
Suggested: Share a few sentences.

levels.0: Word of the day appears in no sentence, spoken or written.
levels.1: Word is repeated back, but the sentence uses it with the wrong meaning or copies the educator's.
levels.2: A sentence of their own containing the word of the day is said aloud and makes sense.
levels.3: Word of the day turns up again later in a new sentence on another topic, with its meaning explained.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm.

rows.name: Think Outside the Box
steps: Suggested: Pose a problem, such as how many uses a paper cup has.
Suggested: Put children into groups of three.
Suggested: Ask each child to say one idea in turn.
Suggested: Write or draw the ideas on a chart.
Suggested: Choose a new idea and share it.

levels.0: Group chart stays blank, with no idea said.
levels.1: Ideas repeat the one obvious use until the educator hints at another.
levels.2: Group puts forward a new idea for the class problem, said aloud and written on the chart.
levels.3: Three different ideas are given for one problem, and one idea is tried with real objects.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C221; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H4.

rows.name: Reading Project
steps: Suggested: Ask each child to pick a book they have read.
Suggested: Draw the cover and three key moments on a sheet.
Suggested: Practise telling it with a partner.
Suggested: Stand and present to the class, holding the book.
Suggested: Take one question from the class.

levels.0: Book is held up, but nothing is said about it.
levels.1: Title and one character are named, but what happens is told only with prompts.
levels.2: A book read is presented in own words, naming the characters and what happens.
levels.3: A favourite part and the reason for choosing it are told, and a classmate's question is answered.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C223; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H4.

rows.name: Class journal entry
steps: Suggested: Choose a class event from the day, such as an experiment or a story.
Suggested: Write two or three sentences about it in the journal.
Suggested: Draw a small picture for the entry.
Suggested: Re-read the entry and add one describing word.
Suggested: Share an entry aloud when invited.
rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C224; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. rows.name: Unscramble Activities
steps: Suggested: Give each child a worksheet with six scrambled words and a picture clue for each.
Suggested: Provide letter tiles.
Suggested: Ask children to slide the letters to make the word.
Suggested: Write the word on the line.
Suggested: Check with a partner.

levels.0: Scrambled letters stay as printed, with no word written on the line.
levels.1: Two- or three-letter words come out right with the picture clue, while longer ones stay mixed.
levels.2: Worksheet lines hold correctly spelled words made by moving the scrambled letters.
levels.3: Scrambled words without picture clues are solved, and a self-made scramble is given to a friend.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C225; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H43.

rows.name: Word Search
steps: Suggested: Give out a grid with a list of six words.
Suggested: Show how to scan across and down.
Suggested: Ask children to circle a word when found.
Suggested: Tick it off on the list.
Suggested: Check with a partner.

levels.0: Grid has no circled word, and the list has no tick.
levels.1: Words reading across are circled, but those reading down are missed.
levels.2: Hidden words in the grid are circled in rows and columns and ticked off the list.
levels.3: A grid with diagonal words is solved, or a short word search is built for a friend.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C226; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H22.

rows.name: Fun Riddles
steps: Suggested: Read a riddle slowly, giving three clues.
Suggested: Ask children to listen with hands in laps.
Suggested: Let them think and whisper to a partner.
Suggested: Ask for the answer aloud.
Suggested: Say which clue helped.

levels.0: No answer is given after the clues, or the answer ignores the clues.
levels.1: An answer is given after the last clue only, with the earlier clues not used.
levels.2: Riddle's answer is said aloud and fits all the clues heard.
levels.3: The clue that gave the answer away is named, and a riddle of their own is told to the class.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C227; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!H15.

rows.name: Memory Drawing
steps: Suggested: Show an object, such as an apple, for ten seconds.
Suggested: Cover it up.
Suggested: Ask children to draw it from memory.
Suggested: Show the object again to compare.
Suggested: Add one missed detail and share the drawings.

levels.0: Paper stays blank after the object is covered.
levels.1: Outline is drawn, but details such as the stalk or colour are missing until the object is shown again.
levels.2: Drawing shows the object's shape and at least three features recalled from memory.
levels.3: A drawing of a more complex object, shown for the same short time, has five features that match.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C228; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!H4.

rows.name: Spelling Bee
steps: Suggested: Pick three- and four-letter words from the class list.
Suggested: Stand in a line or circle.
Suggested: Say the word, use it in a sentence and say it again.
Suggested: Ask the child to spell it aloud letter by letter.
Suggested: Say yes together when correct and rotate.

levels.0: Letters are not spoken, or the word is not attempted.
levels.1: First letters are named in order, but the rest are guessed or mixed up.
levels.2: Given word is spelled aloud, every letter in the right order.
levels.3: A longer word not practised before is spelled aloud and then used in a sentence.

rows.note: Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm.

rows.name: Novel Reading
steps: Suggested: Choose a range of three pages from the class novel.
Suggested: Read them aloud or silently.
Suggested: Close the book.
Suggested: Retell what happened in order to a partner.
Suggested: Ask what happened next.

levels.0: Novel pages are read but nothing is said when asked what happened.
levels.1: One happening is told, with the order mixed up until prompted with what next.
levels.2: Pages read are retold in order with the characters named.
levels.3: Retelling includes a guess about what comes next, with a reason from the text.

rows.note: Named in Curriculum - G1!C236; steps are suggested from the activity name. Steps built from the activity name and the linked objective; syllabus gave only the purpose. Educator should confirm. Also named in AY 2025 - 26 Parent planner!H11.

rows.name: Counting stations: count, group in 2s, 5s, 10s, estimate
steps: Set up counting stations with beans, buttons, plastic animals or counters.
Children move from station to station and count each set.
Group the objects in 2s, 5s and 10s.
Challenge: estimate first, then count.
rows.materials: Beans, buttons, plastic animals, counters, small baskets

levels.0: Silence at the bean station, with no number words spoken while the basket is handled.
levels.1: Counting forward from 1 only, with a pause or restart whenever another starting number is asked for.
levels.2: Bean counts spoken forwards and backwards within 100, starting from a number the educator names.
levels.3: Button groups of 2s, 5s and 10s counted aloud from an unfamiliar start such as 37, in both directions.

rows.name: Addition: concrete objects, strategies and Addition Bingo
steps: Add groups of objects physically.
Teach counting on, number lines and doubles facts.
Play Addition Bingo.
Solve addition puzzles.

levels.0: Counters pushed along the number line one by one for every sum, with no fact spoken straight away.
levels.1: Doubles such as 6 + 6 answered instantly, while other sums within 20 still need the abacus.
levels.2: Addition Bingo calls such as 8 + 7 answered aloud as 15 with no counters or counting on.
levels.3: Bingo-style facts met in a fresh puzzle, such as 9 + 6 in a missing-number box, answered and explained by making ten.

rows.name: Subtraction: take away, counting back, tens frames
steps: Take away counters physically.
Use counting back, number lines and tens frames.
Play with story problems on mini whiteboards.
rows.materials: Blocks, toys, number lines, mini whiteboards

levels.0: Blocks removed and recounted from the start for every subtraction on the whiteboard.
levels.1: Facts from 10 such as 10 - 4 written at once, while 15 - 8 still needs a tens frame.
levels.2: Mini whiteboard answers to 14 - 6 and 17 - 9 written within a few seconds, with no counting back shown.
levels.3: Story problems about toys, such as 16 take away 7, solved with the fact and its matching addition named.

rows.name: Shopping role play and draw-and-solve word problems
steps: Act out 'shopping' stories adding and subtracting money or items.
Draw pictures to solve a story problem.
Solve a mixed set of word problems on mini whiteboards.

levels.0: Story card left unsolved, with no objects moved and no picture drawn on the whiteboard.
levels.1: Shopping items acted out and counted, but the sum or take-away is not written on the whiteboard.
levels.2: Drawn picture of 5 apples and 3 more, with the total 8 written on the mini whiteboard.
levels.3: Coins and a price tag in an unfamiliar story, such as 10 rupees spent from 20, solved with a drawing and a number sentence.

rows.name: Heavy/light, full/empty and which container holds more
steps: Compare objects as heavy or light and containers as full or empty.
Guess, then measure water or sand in cups.
Experiment: which container holds more?

levels.0: Balancing scale left untouched, with no word heavy or light said about the two objects.
levels.1: Heavier object named only after the educator points to the lower pan of the scale.
levels.2: Two objects held in each hand or placed on the scale, with the heavier one named correctly.
levels.3: Cups of water and sand compared, with the one that holds more named and a reason given in own words.

rows.name: Treasure hunt with directions, race positions and AB/ABB/ABC patterns
steps: Give directional clues for a treasure hunt: left, right, forward, backward.
Race and name positions 1st, 2nd, 3rd.
Create and extend AB, ABB and ABC patterns with pattern blocks.

levels.0: Arrow mat steps taken in a random direction, with left and right mixed up at every clue.
levels.1: Forward and backward steps followed on the mat, while left and right need the educator to point.
levels.2: Treasure clues such as left, then forward, followed in order until the hidden object is reached.
levels.3: Fresh route from the classroom door to the library, given with left, right and forward spoken in order.

rows.name: Build-a-number and number battle with bundles of ten
steps: Show quantities as bundles of 10 and counters.
Show the same number in a tens/ones chart.
Discover that the position of a digit changes its value.
Play Build-a-number and Number Battle.

levels.0: Loose counters piled up with no bundles of ten made and no tens or ones named.
levels.1: Bundles of ten made for the tens, while the leftover ones are miscounted or left off the chart.
levels.2: Number 43 shown as 4 bundles of ten and 3 counters, and placed in the right columns of the tens/ones chart.
levels.3: Number Battle cards compared by tens first, with 47 and 52 explained by the digit in the tens place.

rows.note: Grade 1 row of the master summary table. Steps follow the phrases in the 'Place value + comparison' master-summary table of the doc (Maths planning.docx); no further detail in the doc.

rows.name: My Story: baby to now
steps: Look at a baby photo and a current photo (from class or an imagined child).
Sequence picture cards from baby to child.
Share 'When I was small…' in a circle.
Use visuals and gestures; children may speak instead of write.
rows.materials: Baby and current photos, picture cards

levels.0: Picture cards left in a heap, with no card placed under baby time or now.
levels.1: Baby photo and current photo told apart, but the cards between them are placed in the wrong order.
levels.2: Cards for crawling, first tooth and school bag placed in two groups, one for past and one for present.
levels.3: Events from an imagined child's life, such as walking and riding a cycle, sorted into past and present with a reason spoken.

rows.note: Reworded to avoid requiring children's own photographs; use class or story pictures if a family prefers.

rows.name: Match huts and buildings; build a house
steps: Match pictures of a hut and a building.
Compare old and new homes in pictures.
Build a house from blocks or clay.

levels.0: Hut picture and building picture matched to nothing, with no difference between them said.
levels.1: One difference named, such as roof or walls, between the old home and the new home picture.
levels.2: Two home pictures set side by side, with at least two differences named, such as thatch versus concrete.
levels.3: Block house built with a feature that old homes had, with the choice of that feature explained.

rows.name: Arrange routine cards and act out the day
steps: Arrange routine cards from morning to night.
Act out the routine.
Draw one part of the daily sequence.

levels.0: Routine cards left unordered, with no card named for morning or night.
levels.1: Morning and night cards placed at the ends, while the cards in between stay in the wrong order.
levels.2: Routine cards laid from waking to sleeping, with events already done separated from the one happening now.
levels.3: Drawing of one part of another day, such as a holiday, with the order of its events told aloud.

rows.name: Transport then/now matching and message-passing game
steps: Match transport then and now.
Make a pretend phone.
Play a message-passing game.

levels.0: Transport cards left unmatched, with no word then or now said for any vehicle.
levels.1: Bullock cart matched to car, while the pairs for letter and phone stay unmatched.
levels.2: Each old vehicle card paired with its modern one and placed under then or now.
levels.3: Message-passing game round explained by comparing the pretend phone with a whisper chain, saying which is then and which is now.

rows.name: Food sorting, paper doll dress-up and fabric touch
steps: Sort food cards (healthy/unhealthy).
Dress a paper doll.
Touch and feel fabrics.

levels.0: Paper doll dressed with no comparison made between old and present clothes.
levels.1: Food cards sorted into healthy and unhealthy, but no link to food long ago is made.
levels.2: Two pictures of clothes, one old and one present, compared with a difference named, such as fabric or length.
levels.3: Fabric samples felt and sorted by touch, with older and present choices explained, such as rough cotton versus smooth nylon.

rows.name: Community helpers: role play and matching tools
steps: Role play a doctor or educator with props and costumes.
Match helpers to their tools.
Draw a helper.

levels.0: Costumes worn in role play with no helper's workplace named.
levels.1: Doctor's clinic named, while the place for a teacher or postman is left unnamed.
levels.2: Picture of a hospital named and its use told, such as treating the sick.
levels.3: Tool cards matched to helpers and to their workplaces, with the use of each place told for a place not yet met.

rows.name: My Then & Now Book
steps: Gather pictures and drawings from the year.
Make 'My Then & Now Book'.
Show and tell the book to the class.

levels.0: Book pages left blank, with no picture pasted and no drawing of then or now.
levels.1: Pictures pasted on each page, but the then and now labels are missing from the pairs.
levels.2: Facing pages with an old picture and a present picture, plus one difference said during show and tell.
levels.3: Show and tell of a pair not studied in class, such as old and new lamps, with the changes named.

rows.name: Guess Who? and the family ladder
steps: Starter 'Guess Who?': show baby, child, parent, grandparent pictures and ask who is youngest and oldest.
Draw the family ladder on the board: great-grandparents, grandparents, parents, me.
Teach generation, ancestors (above us) and descendants (down from us).
Read the story 'Grandma's Treasure Box' and ask why the objects are special.
Children draw a family tree: grandparents, parents, me.
Exit ticket: circle the oldest generation.
rows.materials: Family picture cards, flashcards, chart paper, stickers, colour pencils

levels.0: Family picture cards pointed at with no word such as grandparent said.
levels.1: Parents and grandparents named, while great-grandparents on the ladder stay unnamed.
levels.2: Grandparents and great-grandparents named on the family ladder, with generation and ancestor said for them.
levels.3: Family tree drawn for a story family, such as Grandma's Treasure Box, with each generation labelled.

rows.name: Family timeline rope and past/present memory match
steps: Show an old photo and a new photo; ask which is older.
Draw a timeline: grandparents as children, parents as children, me as a baby, me today.
Stretch a Past → Present rope and place picture cards in order.
Play Memory Match: old camera/mobile, bullock cart/car, letter/phone.
Think-pair-share: 'Today I learned that family history…'

levels.0: Rope and picture cards left unplaced, with no card put at past or present.
levels.1: Old photo named as older than the new photo, while the timeline strips stay out of order.
levels.2: Memory Match pairs such as bullock cart and car placed on the rope in order from past to present.
levels.3: Think-pair-share sentence beginning family history, sorting a new pair such as letter and phone into past and present.

rows.name: Human family tree and Mystery Family Bag
steps: Assign roles (great-grandparent, grandparent, parent, child) and stand in order as a living family tree.
Fill a bag with an old key, black-and-white photo, toy, letter or recipe card.
Guess who in a family might have used each item and what it tells about the past.

levels.0: Role cards held without standing in a line, with no generation named.
levels.1: Parent and child roles placed in line, while the grandparent and great-grandparent positions are mixed up.
levels.2: Living family tree standing in order, with great-grandparent, grandparent, parent and child each named.
levels.3: Old key or letter from the bag linked to a generation, with a spoken guess about who used it.

rows.name: Save Water pledge poster and sponge-and-bucket game
steps: Make a 'Save Water' pledge poster.
Play blowing games to show wind power.
Play the sponge-and-bucket water transfer game.

levels.0: Pledge poster with no words or drawing and nothing said about water.
levels.1: Poster drawing of a tap, but the way to save water is not spoken aloud.
levels.2: Pledge sentence such as I will turn off the tap written on the poster and read to the class.
levels.3: Sponge-and-bucket game result linked to saving water at home, with a new habit named, such as reusing washing water.

rows.name: Clean the class day, reuse race, seed in a cup
steps: Hold a Clean the class day.
Run a reuse race: best from waste.
Plant a seed in a cup.

levels.0: Waste materials left on the floor with no way to look after the class named.
levels.1: Litter picked up on clean-up day, but the reason is not given in words.
levels.2: Reuse race item made from waste, with one way to care for the class, such as no littering, named.
levels.3: Seed in a cup watered on a chart, with a way to look after plants at home named.

rows.name: Transport sort, wheel printing and paper boat race
steps: Sort and classify transport.
Make wheel printing art.
Build a paper boat and race it.

levels.0: Paper left flat, with no fold made for the boat.
levels.1: Boat fold started with one crease, while the second and third folds are left out or crooked.
levels.2: Paper boat with sharp creases and a hull shape that stays upright at the race.
levels.3: Different shape folded from a fresh sheet, such as a hat or plane, with the folds named in order.

rows.note: Paper boat links to the paper-folding LO; no transport LO exists.

rows.name: Residential and public places sorting
steps: Show pictures and ask 'Can we live here?'.
Teach residential (people live) and public (everyone can use).
Children sort picture cards into residential and public.
Play 'Live or Visit?'.

levels.0: Unsorted picture cards, with no place named during Live or Visit.
levels.1: Home cards placed under residential, while park or market cards stay without a word for what they are used for.
levels.2: Market picture named and its use told, such as buying vegetables, with the card sorted as public.
levels.3: Unseen place such as a bus stand named, sorted as residential or public, with its use said.

rows.name: Where should I go? and My Community chart
steps: Show pictures and ask 'Where would you go if you are sick?'.
Groups build a neighbourhood on chart paper from picture cards.
Each group says 'This is our hospital. Its function is to help sick people.'
Play 'Where Should I Go?': the educator says a need and children hold up the place card.

levels.0: Place card held up with no word for hospital, school or shop said.
levels.1: Hospital named in the chart, but the function sentence is left unfinished.
levels.2: Spoken sentence this is our hospital, its function is to help sick people, matching the place card held up.
levels.3: Need such as buying a book matched to the library or shop card, with the function given in a full sentence.

rows.name: Educator Says and Direction Detective
steps: Play 'Educator Says' with left, right, near and far instructions.
Place a book, pencil, bag and chair around the room.
Ask what is near the pencil and what is to the left of the bag.
Give each child a Direction Detective card with 5 clues.
Exit ticket: ask each child 'What is on your left? What is on your right?'

levels.0: Book, pencil, bag and chair pointed at without left, right, near or far spoken.
levels.1: Near spoken for the pencil, but left or right is mixed up when asked about the bag.
levels.2: Answers such as the pencil is near the bag and the book is to the left said for objects.
levels.3: Exit ticket reply naming what is on own left and right, plus an object in another room.

rows.name: Human compass: North, South, East, West
steps: Mark a large compass on the floor.
Call 'Face North!' and 'Take 2 steps East'.
Play Direction Freeze: when the music stops, point to the called direction.
Complete the My Compass worksheet.

levels.0: Floor compass stood on without any direction word spoken when the music stops.
levels.1: North pointed to on call, while East, South and West are pointed to wrongly.
levels.2: Freeze pose pointing to the called direction, plus a spoken position such as the door is on my left.
levels.3: My Compass worksheet labelled with N, S, E, W and a classroom object placed with its direction and a word such as near.

rows.name: Landmark explorers: treasure hunt map
steps: Explain that a landmark helps us know where we are.
Play 'Guess My Landmark' with clues.
Give a simple school map and walk North, South, West from the star.
Complete the landmark map worksheet.

levels.0: School map left unmarked, with no landmark and no position word said.
levels.1: Star found on the map, but the landmark is named without saying whether it is near or far.
levels.2: Landmark named from the clue in Guess My Landmark, with its place said using near, far, left or right.
levels.3: Worksheet landmark described for a route walked North then West, using near, far or left.

rows.name: Map my journey: Traveller and Guide
steps: Put children in pairs: one Traveller, one Guide.
The Guide gives instructions from a map: start at the school, move East, now North.
The Traveller follows; then swap roles.
Run the Treasure Map Challenge with clues and a hidden card.

levels.0: Treasure card not found, with the Guide giving no direction word.
levels.1: Guide instruction move East given, while the turn to North is missing or reversed.
levels.2: Map instructions spoken in order, such as start at school, move East, now North, with left or right where needed.
levels.3: Swapped roles on a new map, with the Traveller following and the Guide placing the hidden card using near or far.

rows.name: Tell me a story: comic-panel story
steps: Share a simple story (The Hungry Caterpillar) and name beginning, middle, end.
Break a story into 3–4 frames on a folded A4.
Draw the story in sequence cards.
Share and discuss each other's stories.
rows.materials: A4 sheets folded into panels, pencils, crayons, storybooks

levels.0: Folded A4 left without panels filled and no picture of an animal.
levels.1: One or two panels drawn, with the middle or end of the story missing.
levels.2: Three or four frames in order showing an animal story, with a beginning, middle and end.
levels.3: Story about another animal drawn on fresh sequence cards, with each frame told aloud to a peer.

source.cell: Week 25: Creating a Story Through Art

rows.name: Clay forms then painting them
steps: Demonstrate pinch pots and coils.
Roll, pinch and shape a fruit, bowl or animal.
Air-dry the clay.
Paint the dried form with bright colours and fine details.
rows.materials: Air-dry clay, tempera paint, fine brushes

levels.0: Clay left as a lump, with no pinch, roll or shape made.
levels.1: Pinch pot or coil made, but no animal features such as legs or ears are shaped.
levels.2: Clay animal with a body, a head and four legs shaped by hand and painted.
levels.3: Fruit or bowl modelled from a fresh lump, with coils and pinches chosen and named.

source.cell: Week 26–27: Clay and Three-Dimensional Forms; Painting Our Sculptures

rows.name: We are artists: year-end gallery
steps: Review favourite artworks from the year.
Choose 2–3 pieces for display.
Prepare artist cards with names and short reflections.
Host a mini gallery for peers or parents.
rows.materials: Mounting paper, labels, folders, display cloth

levels.0: No artwork is chosen for the gallery.
levels.1: Pieces are chosen, but the artist card is left blank or filled in by the educator.
levels.2: Two or three pieces are mounted with an artist card naming each work and one thing about it.
levels.3: At the gallery, a visitor is told how one piece was made and why it was chosen.

rows.note: No exhibition LO; linked to the nearest art LO. needs_link: no G1 objective covers mounting and presenting work.

rows.name: Group presentations and cooking quiz games
steps: Give group presentations on selected topics.
Play quizzes and interactive games.
Reflect on a favourite cooking experience.

levels.0: Quiz round passed with no sentence about a festival food spoken.
levels.1: Festival food named in the group presentation, but the reason for making it is left out.
levels.2: Sentence such as laddoos are made at Diwali to share sweets said in own words.
levels.3: Reflection on a favourite cooking experience, with a festival food and its reason told for another festival.

rows.note: Review slot; linked to the nearest cooking LO.

rows.name: Tearing and pasting art
steps: Draw a simple shape.
Tear coloured paper into small pieces.
Apply glue.
Paste the pieces inside the outline.
rows.materials: Coloured paper, glue, A4 sheet, crayons

levels.0: Outline drawn with no torn pieces pasted inside.
levels.1: Torn pieces pasted partly inside the outline, with gaps or pieces crossing the line.
levels.2: Shape outline filled completely with torn coloured paper and no glue showing outside.
levels.3: Torn-paper shape made on a fresh outline such as a fish, with the tear-and-paste steps told in order.

rows.name: Leaf printing
steps: Apply paint on one side of a leaf.
Press it onto paper.
Observe the print textures.
rows.materials: Leaves, poster colours, brushes, white paper

levels.0: Paper stays blank after the leaf is pressed, with no print or garden picture on it.
levels.1: Leaf prints appear but are smudged or single, with no garden picture built from several stamps.
levels.2: Several leaf prints on the white paper together form a garden picture with visible vein textures.
levels.3: Poster-colour stamps made from a sponge or cork build a different picture, such as a street scene.

rows.name: Clay fruits and vegetables
steps: Roll clay into shapes.
Make fruits and vegetables.
Add details with fingers.
rows.materials: Air-dry clay or dough, clay mats

levels.0: Clay stays an unshaped lump on the mat.
levels.1: Round or long shapes are rolled, but they look like a fruit or vegetable only with the educator's help.
levels.2: A fruit or vegetable such as a banana or a carrot is shaped with fingers, with a detail like a stalk or lines.
levels.3: A second fruit or vegetable of a different shape is made, and the parts shaped are named.
