rows.name: Bead threading with colour patterns
steps: Watch a threading demonstration.
Make a colour pattern while threading.
Count the beads while threading.
rows.materials: Large beads, shoelaces or thick thread

levels.0: Thread holds beads in no repeating order, with colours or sizes mixed at random.
levels.1: Two beads repeat in order on the shoelace before the colour sequence breaks and wanders.
levels.2: Shoelace shows at least three repeats of a colour unit, such as red, blue, red, blue.
levels.3: Pattern with a three-colour unit is threaded and read aloud bead by bead, with the count said.

rows.name: Paper cup puppets for storytelling
steps: Decorate a paper cup.
Add facial features.
Use the puppet during storytelling.
rows.materials: Paper cups, coloured paper, glue, googly eyes

levels.0: Coloured paper stays flat and unfolded, with no crease or shape made from it.
levels.1: Single crease is made in the coloured paper, and edges do not meet for a finished shape.
levels.2: Coloured paper is folded with matching edges into a shape, such as a hat or ear, glued on the cup.
levels.3: Folds on fresh paper make a different shape, such as a boat, with the folding steps told in order.

rows.name: Sponge painting
steps: Dip a sponge in paint.
Dab gently on paper.
Create patterns.

levels.0: White sheet shows no dabbed marks, only dry paper or one large smear of paint.
levels.1: Dabs cover the sheet in one colour, with no garden shapes such as flowers or grass.
levels.2: Sponge dabs on the white sheet form a garden picture with flowers, grass and leaves in patterns.
levels.3: Sponge shapes cut for a new scene, such as a night sky, give a printed picture with named parts.

rows.name: Decorate a diya or lantern
steps: Paint the diya.
Decorate it with stickers or glitter.
Talk about festivals.
rows.materials: Clay diya or lantern template, decorative materials

levels.0: No word about the festival is spoken when the picture is shown beside the painted diya.
levels.1: One festival word, such as lights or sweets, is said, with no way of celebrating told.
levels.2: Two things done at the festival, such as lighting diyas and sharing sweets, are told from the picture.
levels.3: Shown a picture of a different festival, the telling names what people do and wear there.

rows.name: Cardboard mini house
steps: Join cardboard pieces.
Make windows and a roof.
Decorate the structure.
rows.materials: Cardboard pieces, tape, glue, sketch pens

levels.0: Sketch pen drawing shows no house, or a flat square with no roof or side wall.
levels.1: Front wall and roof are drawn, but no side wall shows the house going back.
levels.2: Pencil house drawing has a front, a side wall and a roof, with slanted lines showing depth.
levels.3: Drawing of a different building, such as a school, uses slanted side lines to show depth too.

rows.name: Robot educator
steps: One adult acts as the robot and does only what is said, literally.
Children instruct the robot to draw a square or to walk to the door.
'Go to the door' fails; 'Turn right, walk four steps, stop' works.
Rewrite instructions until the robot succeeds.

levels.0: Spoken steps like turn right and walk four steps produce no movement towards the door.
levels.1: First instruction is carried out, then the later steps are skipped or done in the wrong order.
levels.2: Turn right, walk four steps and stop are done in the spoken order to reach the door.
levels.3: Spoken steps for a new task, such as drawing a square on the board, are followed in order.

rows.name: A computer hunt around the campus
steps: Walk the campus and find the computers.
Argue about the microwave, the car, the water purifier and the washing machine.
For each, ask: what does it take in, what does it put out? (Worksheet 2)
Pin a drawing at each place on a hand-drawn map.

levels.0: Sorting mat stays empty, with no device picture placed in the input or output group.
levels.1: Device pictures are placed on the mat, but some sit in the wrong group and one stays unplaced.
levels.2: Pictures of the microwave, car and washing machine sit in the correct input or output groups on the mat.
levels.3: Picture of an unseen device, such as a smart speaker, is placed in a group with the reason said aloud.

rows.name: Wired and not wired sort
steps: Sort real objects, then pictures, into joined by wires and not wired (Worksheet 3).
Ask: if there is no wire, how does the message get there?
String wool between children to send a message, then try it without the wool.

levels.0: Worksheet 3 has no device named and no two pictures joined by a line or wool.
levels.1: One device is named from the pictures on Worksheet 3, with no partner device it connects to.
levels.2: Two devices, such as a computer and a printer, are named from the pictures as joined.
levels.3: Two devices from a new picture set, such as a phone and speaker, are named with how they connect.

rows.name: ScratchJr: My name dances
steps: Draw on paper a short sequence for a character to follow.
Write the steps, then find the matching ScratchJr blocks.
When the program does something unexpected, go back to the paper algorithm.
Pin a printed screenshot beside the paper algorithm.

levels.0: Paper algorithm has no step cards in line, and the character's blocks are left unplaced.
levels.1: Several step cards are in order, with one card missing or swapped on the page.
levels.2: Paper algorithm cards lie in the right order and match the ScratchJr blocks on screen.
levels.3: Cards for a new task, such as feeding a pet, are put in order and the steps said aloud.

rows.name: Varnamala Wall

Suggested: Do an oral one-to-one letter-recognition check.
Suggested: Pin the finished wall chart at child height for daily use.

levels.1: Some Hindi letters are written in the notebook, with others reversed, broken or missing the headline.
levels.2: Each Hindi letter from the chart is written in the notebook with its shape and headline complete.
levels.3: Letters from a new set, written from the educator's call without the chart, are formed correctly.

levels.1: Matra card is chosen for the pictured word, but a wrong sign sits on some pairs.
levels.2: Each pictured word is completed by pairing its consonant card with the right matra sign card.
levels.3: Five new pictured words are completed with the right matra, written in the notebook without cards.

levels.1: First two verses come from memory, then a pause and an educator's reminder is needed.
levels.2: Whole poem is recited from memory in order, with the learned actions matching the lines.
levels.3: Poem recited to a different class or at assembly keeps every line and action in order.

levels.1: One line about the family is written beside the drawing, with others left out.

rows.name: Football skills: touches, passing, dribbling, shooting

Shoot at a stationary target.

rows.name: Athletics: running, jumping, throwing and catching
steps: Run and sprint.
Jump and leap.
Throw and catch.

levels.1: Catch is made with one hand or against the chest, after the ball bounces first.
levels.2: Both hands close on the ball thrown by a partner, in at least three of five tries.
levels.3: Throw and catch continue with a smaller ball or a longer distance, both hands still catching.

rows.name: Freeze Tag

Choose one child as the tagger and explain the freeze rule.
Run a short round and swap the tagger.

Observe plant parts.

Make words by joining a letter and a matra (क + ा = का, काला; ग + ी = गी, गीता).
Match half-cards of a letter and a matra to complete the barakhadi.
Colour the matras in the worksheet.

rows.name: Chandrabindu games (चंद्रबिंदु का रिविजन)
steps: Hold the nose and say हाँ, मैं, कहाँ to feel the nasal sound.

Show cards (मां / माँ) and ask children to clap for the correct one.

rows.name: Extra Hindi rhymes with actions
steps: Choose a rhyme such as 'मछली जल की रानी है', 'चंदा मामा दूर के', 'हाथी राजा कहाँ चले' or 'पाँच छोटे बंदर'.
Add clapping, actions and faces; say the rhyme line by line.
Use props (butterfly, fish, moon) and slowly speed up.
Perform in a group.
rows.materials: props, linked YouTube videos in the doc

rows.name: Word-building and matching games in Hindi (शब्द निर्माण, विलोम, एक-अनेक)

Build easy words from letters (क + म = कम) with magnets or cards.

levels.1: Some pairs are matched with help.
